Design decisions

Source: DECISIONS.md

Why the model and the R package are built the way they are. Each entry states a choice, the reason for it, the alternatives considered and set aside, and the tests or validation scripts that check it. The model description says what the model does; this page says why. Validation, derived metrics, the implementation notes and the roadmap are documents of their own.

The entries are grouped by topic and numbered D1 to D54. The model file (inst/slim/malariafwd_vivax.slim), the R code and the model description cite them by number, as in “(D21)”. How to check names tests in tests/testthat/, which devtools::test() runs, and validation scripts in inst/validation/, whose last results are in inst/validation/RESULTS.md.

  • The simulator, a run and its record (D1–D8)
  • Hosts, blood stage and superinfection (D9–D12)
  • The mosquito stage, meiosis and the genetics it makes (D13–D20)
  • Hypnozoites, relapse and the reservoir (D21–D28)
  • Detection, treatment, recrudescence and MDA (D29–D35)
  • Seasonality, vector control and importation (D36–D41)
  • Parameters, outputs and the R interface (D42–D54)

The simulator, a run and its record

What a run is and how it is made: the model in SLiM, one day a tick, launched from R as a subprocess, with a record that repeats it, the outcomes it writes down, and a grid that resumes from what is on disk.

D1 — The package is the engine and the readers of its ground truth

Decision. malariafwd is the SLiM model, the R functions that run it one simulation or a whole grid at a time, and the readers of what a run records: loaders, epidemiological and genetic summaries, ground-truth IBD, marker genotypes painted on the genealogy, and plots, one function to a question (D54). Research analyses built on it sit outside the package. The package and its model share the name (malariafwd_vivax.slim), which leaves room for species other than P. vivax.

Why. The package holds what every use of the model needs, the engine and the readers of its truth, and nothing that belongs to one study, so it does not move with research in progress.

Alternatives considered. The engine alone would be too thin to use: every user would rebuild the IBD and the metrics a run is read with. The engine with a study’s analysis framework would tie the package to that research.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-exports.R lists the exports exactly.

D2 — SLiM runs as a subprocess, and Python is reached through one check

Decision. run_sim() starts slim as a process through processx, with no shell, and gives it every parameter as a -d NAME=value constant; the model writes its own output files, and SLiM’s console output goes whole to run.log. The binary is the one MALARIAFWD_SLIM names, or slim on the PATH, and must be SLiM 5.2 or newer: the model is tested on 5.2, and 5.0 and 5.1 give different output for the same seed. The same model file runs without R, with slim -d, and its initialize() then makes the checks R makes (D43). Its per-event narration prints only under VERBOSE = TRUE: a quiet log holds little beyond SLiM’s start-up, the genome line and the closing banner, and a run’s events, states and genealogy are the same either way. Python serves only to read tree sequences, and reticulate is suggested rather than required, so running the model and reading a run’s tables need no Python. The tree-sequence functions reach tskit (>= 1.0) and numpy through reticulate behind one check (R/python.R), which declares the modules before Python starts: a Python the user chose is used as it is, and with none chosen reticulate builds its own environment with them. A check that finds everything holds for the session. A function that cannot reach the modules stops, naming itself, with class malariafwd_no_python and one paragraph: the Python in use and how it came to be used, what is missing, and what to do. tskit_available() answers without a condition, and check_setup() reports SLiM, the model and the Python side.

Why. Launching a process costs little beside a run, which takes tens of seconds for 150 hosts over three years (MODEL_DESCRIPTION 16.6), and a model that writes its own files needs nothing from R while it runs. Without a shell, the quotes of an Eidos string, such as OUTDIR='.' or a SIM_ID with an apostrophe, reach SLiM as written. One model file cannot drift from a quiet copy of itself; the quiet default keeps a sweep’s logs small, and a single run can still be narrated to debug it. Declaring the modules changes nothing for a Python the user chose and is what reticulate needs to build its own, and one check gives every function the same modules and the same message.

Alternatives considered. slimr adds a layer that parses SLiM’s output. system2() passes the arguments through a shell, which strips the quotes of an Eidos string. A separate quiet model file would drift from the narrated one, and removing the narration would lose the debugging mode. Declaring the modules when the package loads would add tskit to reticulate’s environment for a user who never reads a tree sequence, and py_module_available() alone is FALSE until Python has started.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R (an apostrophe and a space in the output path and the SIM_ID, and a non-ASCII SIM_ID in a C locale), tests/testthat/test-slim.R (a SLiM older than 5.2 is refused), tests/testthat/test-python.R (every branch of the Python check, and check_setup()) and tests/testthat/test-run-dir.R (a run’s key ignores VERBOSE).

D3 — Time advances in daily ticks, and a duration parameter is the mean of a geometric duration

Decision. One tick is one day, in SLiM’s nonWF order. reproduction() draws the day’s hypnozoite activations, as relapses, and deaths; clones the hypnozoite batch of an import that arrived the day before; runs the bites, with uptake and meiosis in the mosquito and inoculation in the host; and re-expands the suppressed clones whose day has come, as recrudescences. early() removes the emptied hypnozoite batches and the clones the day’s recrudescences replaced, which SLiM cannot kill in reproduction(); gives the courses that are due; clears blood-stage clones; kills and replaces mosquitoes; gives an MDA round on MDA_TICK; brings the day’s imports; and ends the run if no parasite is left and none can still come (D5). late() writes the day’s rows of state.tsv, and on the last day the tree sequence. A duration parameter D, such as MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION or MOSQ_LIFESPAN, is the mean of a geometric duration: the event happens each day with probability 1/D. TREATMENT_DELAY and, by default, MEAN_RECRUD_DELAY follow the same rule from the day after the case or the suppression, so each lasts at least a day (D32). BITING_RATE, ALPHA_ACTIVATE, MU_HYPNOZOITE and DELTA_LATENCY are daily probabilities, so the waiting times they set are geometric too; EIP_DAYS and GAMETOCYTE_DELAY are delays of a set number of days. A mosquito bites at most once a day, so vivax_params() warns when BITING_RATE times its seasonal, intervention and resurgence multipliers passes 1 on a day of the run.

Why. Every duration has one reading, and each parameter means what it says: at the default of 60 days, blood-stage clearance is White et al. (2014)’s rate of 1/60 a day applied as a daily probability, and an infection lasts 60 days on average. Two steps sit where SLiM requires: imports arrive in early(), since reproduction() runs only while a parasite exists and an import must be able to seed an empty population (D38), and courses are given in early(), the first point at which a genome made in that day’s reproduction() can be seen, so radical cure reaches the batch the case’s own bite seeded (D31).

Alternatives considered. Converting each duration with 1 - exp(-1/D), natural in a continuous-time model, would not fit a model that steps in days and whose other processes are daily probabilities already, and it would give a parameter of D days a mean of about D + 1/2 (2.54 days at D = 2).

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R (founder infections with MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION = 2 last 2 days on average), tests/testthat/test-treatment.R (the treatment and recrudescence delays have mean D and last at least a day) and tests/testthat/test-params.R (the biting warning follows the model’s own seasonal, intervention and boost timeline).

D4 — Every genome is remembered in the tree sequence before it is killed

Decision. Every path that removes a genome first calls treeSeqRememberIndividuals(permanent = RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY): natural blood-stage clearance; a case course or an MDA round that clears a clone, a subpatent one included; the removal of a hypnozoite batch emptied by activation and death, by radical cure or by MDA; the death of a mosquito, with the products it carries; and the removal of a clone that a recrudescence has replaced. RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY is TRUE by default, so plasmo.trees keeps every genome a run made. With FALSE the genomes are remembered without the permanent flag and most earlier ones leave the tree sequence: ibd_pairs() lists a requested id it does not hold in missing, warns once and looks it up as NA, and asking only for such ids is an error.

Why. IBD between a recurrence and an infection that has already cleared, which recurrences() reports and every relapse-to-origin comparison rests on, needs the cleared genome’s ancestry, and a genome killed without being remembered can be simplified out of the tree, its ancestry with it. FALSE is for runs that will never ask about earlier infections.

How to check. inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R (the logged cases are in the tree sequence), tests/testthat/test-ibd.R (every relapse is found, at IBD 1, with the batch it woke from) and tests/testthat/test-no-parasite.R (with RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY = FALSE, the readers give their NA rows, and the error names the setting).

D5 — A run that dies out, and one that never starts, are results the run writes down

Decision. A run goes extinct on the first tick on which no parasite is left in any host or mosquito, hypnozoites included, and no importation is still to come. It ends on that tick, and records it even when that tick is its last day: it writes its tree sequence, its events.tsv and state.tsv stop there, and its params.tsv ends with an EXTINCT_TICK row, which load_run() reads into extinct_tick (NA for a run that did not go extinct) and run_sim() reports. A founder-free run whose imports all fail to establish a parasite, by chance (a Poisson rate that draws none, imports that take in neither compartment) or because its settings let none take (P_PRIMARY = 0 with a hypnozoite batch mean of 0, an import rate of 0 throughout its window), never starts: it ends on the first tick after its last import day but not before tick 10, and in any case on its last day, writes its outputs as an extinct run does, and ends params.tsv with a NEVER_STARTED row, which load_run() reads as never_started = TRUE. run_grid() gives each outcome a column and counts its cells in a message of its own; a cell that never started is ok. An import is still to come until the run passes LAST_IMPORT_DAY, the last day of the run on which one can arrive (0 if none): a window inside the run counts to its last day even while its rate is 0, and a pulse or window outside the run brings nothing. The model’s start-up check and its end-of-day check read that one constant, and R works out the same days. A founder-free set with no import path inside the run is refused before SLiM starts (D42). Every reader takes a run with no parasite: its tables have their usual columns and no rows, its counts are 0, and a quantity that needs a parasite is NA; the summaries of a window count the days after an extinction as days with no parasite (D49).

Why. Fade-out and a failure of importation are results: how often imports fail to seed an outbreak is itself worth counting. Every later tick would be empty, so the run ends there. Recording an extinction on the last day too means NA says only that a run did not go extinct, which a grid counting extinctions needs, and the two outcomes are facts of the run rather than parameters, so every run’s parameter set has the same names. One constant for the import days keeps the checks from disagreeing about whether an import can still come.

Alternatives considered. Stopping a run that never started with an error would lose a sweep’s cell to chance. Recording it as an extinction would confuse a run that never had a parasite with one whose parasites died out. Refusing a founder-free set whose imports cannot take would remove a legitimate null arm of a grid, as a closed border is, whose honest outcome is that it never started.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R (a run that dies out, also with imports set outside it; founder-free runs whose imports never take, and the tick each import schedule ends on), tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-slim.R (a founder-free set with no import path inside the run is refused, by R and by the model run directly), tests/testthat/test-load.R and tests/testthat/test-no-parasite.R (extinct and never-started runs load with the usual columns, and every reader takes them).

D6 — A run directory holds one whole run or what it held before

Decision. run_sim() writes a run into a new directory beside outdir, starts SLiM there (OUTDIR is '.') on the run’s own copy of the model, model.slim, and moves the directory to outdir only once SLiM has exited 0, the four outputs exist and DONE has been written, last. A run that fails, times out or is interrupted goes to <outdir>.failed with its run.log, which holds SLiM’s error output too; SLiM is stopped if R dies, which leaves an <outdir>.partial-* directory to delete by hand. DONE records when the run finished, how long it took, its seed, a key of its parameters and seed (the md5 of the sorted arguments SLiM is given, without OUTDIR and VERBOSE), the md5 of the model, the versions and the size of every file. A directory without DONE, or whose files have changed since, loads with complete = FALSE, and every reader given it warns once per directory per session (class malariafwd_incomplete_run). An outdir that holds this run is returned with skip_existing = TRUE; one that holds any run, finished or not, is replaced with overwrite = TRUE once the new run is in place, and is otherwise refused (class malariafwd_outdir_in_use); one that holds other files is never used, and only a run’s own files are ever deleted.

Why. A run directory is ground truth: it should hold one whole run or none, say which, and not be replaced by accident. Writing beside outdir makes the final move a rename within one file system.

Alternatives considered. Deleting outdir first would let a failed run destroy the one before it. Writing in place with DONE alone would still leave a failed run’s files mixed with those of the run before it. Loaders that refuse a directory without DONE would lock out runs started with slim directly, which have none. Hashing every output into DONE would cost time, where the sizes catch a truncated copy at no cost. A marker written by the model cannot know that R holds the whole run. Replacing a run by default would let a script run again replace ground truth without a word.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run-dir.R (a run stopped part-way leaves outdir as it is; outdir appears only when the run has finished; SLiM’s error output reaches run.log; a run is reused or replaced only when asked; other files are never touched; DONE’s rows and key; an incomplete directory warns once).

D7 — A run’s record rebuilds the run, and one seed gives one set of tables

Decision. params.tsv holds every resolved parameter, with ACTUAL_SEED, the SLiM and package versions, the derived GENOME_LENGTH, N_CHROMOSOMES and RECOMB_WITHIN, and the outcome rows of D5; floats are written to the 15 significant digits run_sim() passes SLiM, a whole one with its decimal point (10.0) and an exponent form as printf writes it (7.4e-07). vivax_params() stores each value in its default’s type and as SLiM is given it: a count or a scheduling day as an integer, and a double as the value of its 15-digit text. load_params() reads the file back into the vivax_params() set that made the run, every parameter of its type and none validated, so run_sim(load_params(run), seed = run$seed, outdir = tempfile()) repeats a run started from R whenever each of its non-zero floats lies between 1e-130 and 1e15 in magnitude. The seed, the versions, the derived genome and the outcomes are typed fields of the load_run() object instead. A params.tsv that lacks a parameter, or holds a row that is neither a parameter nor a record row, loads with the default or without the row and warns once per directory per session (class malariafwd_params_mismatch). run_sim() gives SLiM the seed both as -s and as SEED, which the model sets, so the tree sequence’s provenance and params.tsv agree, and cmdline.txt holds SLiM’s arguments, so slim run with them beside model.slim repeats the run. Every genome’s x, y and z are set to 0 where it is made, in setHostGenome() or tagMosqProduct(), so two runs of one seed give the same tree-sequence tables, all but the provenance row, where SLiM records the run’s date, its duration and the memory it used.

Why. A run’s record should be the run, and a parameter set should hold what the run is given; the record rows describe a run rather than set it, so they belong to the run object. A default filled in for a missing parameter is not a setting of that run, hence the warning. SLiM writes each individual’s coordinates into the tree sequence even in a non-spatial model and leaves them undefined until a model sets them, and a new individual can take over the memory of one that died, so unset coordinates would make two runs of one seed differ in their tables while their events.tsv and state.tsv agree.

Alternatives considered. Seventeen digits, or hexadecimal floats, would carry any double exactly, but Eidos cannot read hexadecimal floats, and seventeen digits print values with digits nobody set (0.1 as 0.10000000000000001); at 15, the set, its record and what SLiM is given still hold one value. The record rows in an attribute of the set would be lost to most list operations. Validating on load would let a file’s content stop a reader; run_sim() checks a set before it runs. Setting the coordinates once a day would record a genome made and remembered on one day before they are set.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-params.R (a double is stored as SLiM is given it, each value has its default’s type, a rebuilt set is the set), tests/testthat/test-slim.R (params.tsv records floats to 15 significant digits, from R and from a direct run), tests/testthat/test-run.R (the set read from a run is the set that made it, a run from it gives the same files, and the record is typed), tests/testthat/test-load.R (types, and a file that does not match warns once), tests/testthat/test-run-dir.R (the directory repeats its own run), tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R (coordinates are 0 where SLiM reuses a dead genome’s memory, and two runs of one seed give the same tables) and inst/validation/check_parameters.R (one seed gives a byte-identical event log).

D8 — A grid checks every cell first, runs one future per cell, resumes from disk and records itself

Decision. run_grid() rebuilds every parameter set and checks every cell’s directory against what run_sim() would do with it before any cell starts: a refused set, or a cell that holds another run, one that did not finish or files that are not a run’s, stops the grid with them named. A set’s name names its cells’ directories (<set>_seed<seed>), so names must differ, also ignoring case, and be usable as directory names; seeds must be distinct whole numbers. Each cell is one future::future(), labelled with the cell so that an error from a lost worker names it, and runs under the caller’s plan or, with workers, a multisession plan for the call; it takes no seed, since the cells draw no random numbers in R, and the caller’s random-number stream is left as it is. A cell that already holds its run is not run again (skip_existing = TRUE), so a second call resumes a grid that stopped part-way, and overwrite = TRUE runs the cells of an edited set again. A cell that fails does not stop the grid: its directory is left as it is, its files go to <cell>.failed, and the grid warns, with the reason in the error column. The calling session writes grid.tsv at the end, with paths relative to the grid’s directory: each cell’s outcome, versions and key, and every parameter as SLiM is given it, which load_grid() reads. The result is a data.table, one row per cell, with the parameters that vary between the sets.

Why. A grid is launched, left and launched again after a failure: it should cost only the cells that are missing, say what it holds, and not run half its cells before saying what is wrong. A future plan runs the same call on a laptop’s cores or a cluster’s nodes, and cells run by other means, such as one run_sim() per job of a job array, are recorded by calling run_grid() with the same sets and seeds afterwards, which runs nothing.

Alternatives considered. A grid class would misreport subsets, since data.table keeps a subclass through subsetting. Keying a cell on the SLiM version would let an upgrade invalidate every finished grid; the versions are recorded instead. Workers writing grid.tsv would race on one file. parallel::mclapply() forks on Unix only and has no path to a cluster. furrr or future.apply would each add a dependency for what one future per cell does.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-grid.R (names, seeds, the caller’s stream, resuming, an edited set, grid.tsv and load_grid() across a moved directory, a failed cell), the grid tests in tests/testthat/test-run.R, and part 3 of inst/validation/check_parameters.R, which runs a grid with two workers on the installed package.

Hosts, blood stage and superinfection

The host side: how long a clone lasts, how many a host can take, which of its parasites a mosquito can see, and when a clone can pass parasites on.

D9 — A blood-stage clone clears on a daily draw, with no age ceiling

Decision. Each patent blood-stage clone clears on its own each day, in early(), with probability 1/MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION, so a host carrying several clones loses them independently and its MOI decays rather than collapsing at once. A clone cannot clear on the day its blood stage began, so its blood stage lasts a geometric number of days, at least one, with mean MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION (D3). No ceiling clears a clone by age. A subpatent clone makes no draw, and a recrudescence is a new clone (D33); since no draw depends on age, a recrudescence clears as a new infection does, and a clone that cycles through suppression has no limit on its total persistence. MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION must be finite and at least 1, in vivax_params() and in the model’s initialize().

Why. The default of 60 days is White et al. (2014)’s clearance rate, 1/60 a day, used as a daily probability. A ceiling would cut off the geometric tail, so the realised mean would fall short of MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION and the parameter would mean something other than what it says. Nor would it guard against anything: the only means that stop clearance, a negative or an infinite one, are refused by the requirement that the mean be finite and at least 1, which the daily probability needs anyway, since below 1 it would exceed 1.

Alternatives considered. A high ceiling as a safety net, 365 days say: it would still cut the tail wherever MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION is long, and guard against nothing the parameter check does not already refuse.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R checks, with founders only, that clones last a geometric time with the parameter’s mean and that none is forced to clear at a set age. tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R refuse a mean below 1 or an infinite one, and tests/testthat/test-slim.R a mean below 1 in a run started directly with slim -d.

D10 — One superinfection gate for every new inoculation, counting the clones a host gained that day

Decision. A host already carrying MAX_MOI blood-stage lineages, patent or subpatent, takes no new inoculation, a local bite or an import alike: the whole inoculation is skipped, blood-stage primary and hypnozoite batch, so a full host’s reservoir is not topped up either. A bite is checked whatever the host’s infectious state, before its P_TRANS_VH draw, so a refused bite makes no such draw; the refusal stops only the host’s inoculation, and on the same bite an infectious host can still infect the mosquito. Each host keeps a list of the lineages of the blood-stage clones it gained earlier in the day, by a relapse or a bite, emptied at the start of each day’s reproduction(), and a bite’s check counts them with the clones the host carries; an import arrives in early(), after the day’s bites, so its check finds them among the host’s clones. A bite on a host whose only clones arrived that day is inoculated like any other: only the mosquito’s uptake needs a clone the host already shows, and with none it is skipped without a draw. Relapses bypass the gate, so realised MOI can exceed MAX_MOI; so can a bite that delivers several genotypes, which is admitted whole, and a founder host whose genome is a copy of another founder’s (D40). A refused import is logged as vh_inoculation_import_no_take; a refused bite leaves no row. MAX_MOI is at least 1, in vivax_params() and in the model’s initialize().

Why. MAX_MOI is about parasite burden, not about what a microscope or a mosquito can see, so subpatent clones count (D11), and it is one rule for every inoculation, whatever its route. The order of the bites within a day is an artefact of the loop and should decide neither whether a bite counts nor whether the cap holds; SLiM adds a clone made in reproduction() to its host only when that callback ends, so without the day’s list the clones a host gained earlier that day would be hidden from its later bites. MAX_MOI = 0 would refuse every inoculation, an empty host’s included, where 1 already means no superinfection. At the default of 20 the gate is a guard that seldom binds, COI being typically 1 to 3; set low, it becomes the quantity a run measures, as the roadmap warns.

Alternatives considered. Gating a bite only when the host has an infectious clone: two gates for one rule about parasite burden, under which, at SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY = 0, a host whose clones are all subpatent would take bites past the cap while refusing imports. Counting only the clones a host shows: a second bite on the same day would get a second clone in even at MAX_MOI = 1.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R: at MAX_MOI = 2, with no relapses and one genotype per bite, no host ever carries more than 2 blood-stage lineages; at P_TRANS_VH = 1, with case management and no host full, each host’s infectious bites a day are its inoculations that day. tests/testthat/test-run.R: at MAX_MOI = 1 no import lands in a host that still carries its clone, and the refusals are logged; at SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY = 0, with every course failing into subpatency, no bite reaches a host once its clone is suppressed. tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-slim.R refuse MAX_MOI = 0, the second in a run started directly with slim -d. inst/validation/check_parameters.R checks that MAX_MOI = 2 lowers mean COI.

D11 — Patency, infectiousness and capacity are three separate counts

Decision. The model asks three questions of a host’s blood stage and answers each with its own count of distinct lineages; none counts hypnozoite batches. getActiveLineageCount() counts the patent lineages: the COI, moi_active in state.tsv, which leaves out a subpatent clone, since it is undetectable and in no episode. getTransmissibleLineageCount() counts the lineages that can infect a mosquito, subpatent ones included whenever SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY > 0; it sets the host’s infectious tag, the tag column of state.tsv, and is the test the bite loop makes before a mosquito can take up parasites. Which of those clones a mosquito draws from is settled at each uptake: each subpatent clone joins with probability SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY, and the gametocyte gate applies (D12). getBloodStageLineageCount() counts every blood-stage lineage present, patent or subpatent, which is the MAX_MOI question for an import; for a bite, getCapacityLineageCount() adds the lineages the host gained earlier that day (D10). Each call site asks the question it means. At the shipped defaults no clone is ever subpatent and the three agree; they part once a failed course can leave a clone suppressed (D33).

Why. Subpatency separates three properties that coincide without it. A suppressed clone is undetectable, so it is in no episode and no part of the COI. It can still infect a mosquito, if less well than a patent clone: in the feeding studies Koepfli et al. (2021) compile, microscopy-positive carriers are 5 to 10 times as infective as submicroscopic ones. And it still occupies its host, since MAX_MOI is about parasite burden (D10).

Alternatives considered. The patent count for all three questions, or a separate infectious tag with the bite loop still testing the patent count. Either way the bite loop passes over a host whose clones are all subpatent, so that host never infects a mosquito whatever SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY says, and nothing shows it: the subpatent compartment is usually small, so a missing route looks like a minor one. The patent count would also let a host whose clones are subpatent take bites past MAX_MOI.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R refuses a bite on a host at MAX_MOI = 1 whose clone is suppressed at SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY = 0, a host the infectiousness count leaves out; tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R checks that a host with only hypnozoite batches is not infectious, and tests/testthat/test-load.R that every host tagged infectious carries a patent or subpatent clone. The uptake route itself has no test of its own; to check it, join each hv_uptake_* row on day T to its host’s state.tsv row on day T − 1, in a run whose courses fail into subpatency: uptakes from hosts with moi_active = 0 number 0 at SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY = 0 and rise with it.

D12 — Gametocyte gating is in the model and acts as the identity at the shipped defaults

Decision. A blood-stage clone can infect a mosquito only from gametocyte_ready_tick, its onset plus GAMETOCYTE_DELAY days, and only if it carries gametocytes, which a Bernoulli draw at P_GAMETOCYTE decides once for the clone and keeps. Every new clone, a relapse’s and a recrudescence’s included, starts its own delay and makes its own draw. A clone first meets the bite loop the day after its onset, since a clone made in reproduction() joins its host only when that callback ends and an import arrives in early(), after the bites; so a GAMETOCYTE_DELAY of 0 acts as 1. A mosquito that bites a host none of whose clones pass the gate takes up nothing. The gate applies after the subpatent clones have been thinned at SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY (D11); at the shipped GAMETOCYTE_DELAY = 0 and P_GAMETOCYTE = 1 it passes every clone and draws no random number, so a default run is identical to one without the gate.

Why. Vivax gametocytes appear early, at or near the onset of symptoms rather than after the 10 to 12 days falciparum gametocytes take to mature (Bousema & Drakeley 2011; Koepfli et al. 2021), so infectiousness runs close to the blood stage, and a realistic setting, a delay of 2 to 3 days with carriage of about 0.9, lies near the identity. The parameters are there for the sensitivity analysis that the roadmap calls for. The delay is one value for every clone: at a few days against a 60-day mean blood stage (D9), its variance can do little to the dynamics.

Alternatives considered. Removing the two parameters: they are the knob a sensitivity analysis of gametocyte timing and carriage needs. Shipping the realistic setting as the default: it would move the transmission at which NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH is fitted (D21) for little gain, the setting being close to the identity. A delay drawn for each infection, from a Poisson or a uniform over 0 to 3 days: simple to add, but it would matter only to a question about the delay’s tail, such as the share of early transmitters or how the timing of treatment meets infectiousness.

How to check. inst/validation/check_parameters.R runs a configuration with GAMETOCYTE_DELAY = 3 and P_GAMETOCYTE = 0.8 through its structural checks; no check measures the gate’s effect on uptake.

The mosquito stage, meiosis and the genetics it makes

Where the genetics come from: how much a mosquito takes up, what meiosis does to it, the genome it happens on, and how relatedness is read back out of the recorded genealogy.

D13 — Uptake and inoculation counts are zero-truncated, and their lambdas are pre-truncation rates

Decision. A successful blood meal forms a zero-truncated Poisson(LAMBDA_OOCYSTS) number of oocysts, each its own meiosis (D14), negative binomial with variance λ + λ²/K when K_OOCYSTS > 0. An infectious bite samples a zero-truncated LAMBDA_SPOROZOITES number of a mosquito’s post-EIP products, with replacement and weighted by spz_weight, and repeat draws of one lineage collapse to a single genotype. A lambda of 0 gives exactly one. Both default to 2, so an uptake forms 2.31 oocysts and a bite samples 2.31 products on average, and a bite delivers several genotypes, co-transmitted, whenever it draws more than one lineage the mosquito carries. Both lambdas are pre-truncation rates, not mean counts: uptake_moments(lambda, k) gives the moments a setting produces and uptake_calibrate(mean, var) converts a target mean, and optionally a variance, into the lambda and K to set. An uptake whose 10,000 gamma-Poisson tries all give 0 draws its count exactly, by inversion of the zero-truncated negative binomial.

Why. Truncation, not inflation, is the right family: P_TRANS_HV and P_TRANS_VH already decide whether the event happens, so the zeros of a feeding dataset are represented upstream and inflating here would count one failure twice. Between-donor gametocytaemia variation is likewise emergent, so K_OOCYSTS carries only the residual within-feed overdispersion that vivax membrane feeds show (a zero-inflated negative binomial describes 96 direct membrane-feeding assays of 22,236 mosquitoes, Miura et al. 2020); the sampling scheme follows Wong et al. (2018). Conditioning away the zeros pulls the realised mean up — λ = 1 gives 1.58, λ = 2 gives 2.31, and λ = 2 with K = 1 gives 3.0 — so a lambda cannot be read off a reported mean oocyst count, and the two helpers make that conversion explicit instead of leaving it to the reader. The exact draw is reached by 37% of uptakes where a positive count is one draw in 10,000 (LAMBDA_OOCYSTS about 1e-4, at any K) and by fewer than one in a million above about 0.003. No study has measured how many genotypes a natural bite delivers, so the defaults of 2 are an assumption: they let co-transmission happen in every default run, at a modest rate, and the roadmap lists both lambdas for sensitivity analysis.

Alternatives considered. Settling for a single oocyst when the tries run out; it would make the count less dispersed than uptake_moments() reports. Drawing the count by inversion wherever a positive count is rare; at the smallest K_OOCYSTS the model accepts, 0.001, ordinary settings already need about 110 tries per positive count, so the exact draw would displace the rejection draw where rejection works well. Both lambdas at 0 by default, one oocyst per uptake and one genotype per bite: co-transmission, and the sibling genotypes it brings into one host, would be absent from every default run.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R (the exact draw’s mean and variance against uptake_moments()); tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R (edge settings, among them the small K_OOCYSTS that uptake_calibrate() can return, run to the end); inst/validation/calibrate_nu.R (the share of bites that deliver more than one genotype, at each batch mean it tries).

D14 — An outcrossed oocyst gives a full tetrad by per-chromosome four-strand meiosis, with meiosis I pairing at the centromeres

Decision. Each oocyst draws two gametes independently and uniformly, with replacement, from the host’s gametocyte pool, and outcrosses exactly when the two differ, so selfing and outcrossing emerge; the pool’s Simpson index is logged as p_outcross and drives nothing. An outcrossed zygote’s two genomes replicate into four chromatids per chromosome; chiasmata fall at the union of two gamete-rate breakpoint draws within each chromosome, each joining a random chromatid of each parent; meiosis I sends the two chromatids carrying the same parent at the chromosome’s annotated centromere to one pole, drawn independently for each chromosome; meiosis II gives one of them to each product of that pole. The four products therefore form two pairs of meiosis II sisters on every chromosome, and every product carries the full map of crossovers. A product with no switch at all is a whole copy of its starting parent and keeps that parent’s lineage. A selfed oocyst’s four identical products are stored as one object with spz_weight = 4, which the sampling at a bite corrects for (D13).

Why. This is canonical four-strand meiosis without chromatid interference, and independent uniform gamete draws give both the marginal P(outcross) = 1 − Σpᵢ² and the correct pairing P(i,j) ∝ pᵢpⱼ (Wong et al. 2018), which rolling outcrossing first and then picking two distinct lineages would not. The centromeres are the centres of the features PVP01_CEN01–PVP01_CEN14 of the PvP01 annotation (Sanger/GeneDB, released with Auburn et al. 2016), held as fractions of each chromosome so that GENOME_MODE = "core" keeps them (D16); the split barely depends on where they sit (chromosome midpoints give sisters 0.614 and the other pairs 0.193, the annotated positions 0.603 and 0.198). A sequenced P. falciparum tetrad supports the pairing: read against the 3D7 centromere annotation, its four products form two pairs that carry the same parent at all 13 centromeres that can be read, sharing 0.67 of the genome against the other pairs’ 0.17, where the model gives 0.60 and 0.20; six further pairs of cells in the same study’s sibling groups carry the same parent at every readable centromere (Nkhoma et al. 2020, Figure 6 and Data S3; the centromere readings are ours, from the published figures). Since IBD and relatedness methods are scored against this genealogy as ground truth, the shape of same-oocyst sharing is itself a modelling target.

Alternatives considered. A random deal of each chromosome’s four chromatids to the four products, as in the simulator of Wong et al. (2018); it drops meiosis I and makes every same-oocyst pair look alike, around 1/3 with sd about 0.08, which would flatter the methods scored against the model. Pairing the products without centromeres, by a deal fixed at each chromosome’s start; it gives sisters 0.50 and the other pairs 0.25, so the centromere positions matter. Gene conversion, which the same tetrad shows in two tracts (872 bp and 181 kb); one tetrad gives no rate to fit. An obligate chiasma per bivalent; no source supports one for P. vivax, and it would move sisters to about 0.58 and the other pairs to about 0.21, about twice the effect of the centromere positions.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R runs the model’s own seedTetrad() for 400 tetrads with a probe at every centromere: 2:2 segregation at every probe, two sister pairs per oocyst carrying the same parent at all 14 centromeres, sister and other pairs’ sharing against 1/3 + (2/3)e^(−3rt) and 1/3 − (1/3)e^(−3rt) at map distance rt from the centromere, each product’s crossovers against the map, the reciprocal pairing on chromosomes with one crossover, and the same centromere fractions in "core" mode and with a CHROMOSOMES subset. inst/validation/audit_arg_recombination.R and inst/validation/audit_arg_junctions.R check the same machinery in a run’s recorded genealogy.

D15 — The 14 chromosomes are one concatenated linkage group

Decision. The genome is one SLiM chromosome holding the PvP01 chromosomes end to end, with the within-chromosome rate along each and r = 0.5 at each of the 13 junctions. seedTetrad() discards the junction breakpoint draws and assorts the chromosomes itself at the centromeres (D14), which gives every product exactly r = 0.5 across a junction. The model holds the chromosome starts on the concatenated map, and chrom_map() recovers the layout in R from the genome parameters the run recorded, so the segment functions can cut at the junctions (D18).

Why. One concatenated linkage group is genetically equivalent to explicit chromosomes for every IBD quantity the package reports, and it keeps one .trees file per run. SLiM’s explicit multi-chromosome mode writes a directory of per-chromosome tree sequences, so the whole IBD pipeline would have to aggregate across 14 files; its one unique payoff, per-chromosome trees for chromosome-level selection scans, is of no use in a model with no mutation and no selection (D17).

Alternatives considered. Explicit SLiM chromosomes — that payoff against an IBD pipeline spread over 14 files per run.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R (a product changes parent at a junction with probability 1/2); inst/validation/audit_arg_recombination.R (breakpoint spikes at all 13 junctions on a uniform within-chromosome background) and inst/validation/audit_arg_junctions.R (a product’s parent decorrelates across a junction, φ ≈ 0, while staying linked over 200 kb within a chromosome, φ ≈ 0.71); tests/testthat/test-run.R (the chrom_map() lengths sum to the genome length the run recorded).

D16 — GENOME_MODE is a coordinate switch, and one uniform crossover rate serves both modes

Decision. GENOME_MODE = "full", the default, gives the exact PvP01 chromosome lengths, 24.2 Mb; "core" gives 90% of each, a proxy for the subtelomere-masked core genome of the MalariaGEN Pv4 release, about 21.8 Mb. Both modes use one uniform within-chromosome crossover rate of 7.4e-7 per bp. RECOMB_RATE overrides that rate for sensitivity analysis, and CHROMOSOMES chooses which of the 14 chromosomes to simulate.

Why. 7.4e-7 per bp (13.5 kb/cM) is the euchromatic core rate of Jiang et al. (2011), a P. falciparum estimate used for want of a comparable published vivax genome-wide map; the genome-wide figure (9.6 kb/cM) is higher only because it averages in hyper-recombinogenic subtelomeres, which a uniform map does not place spatially, so spreading it everywhere would overstate recombination exactly where the analysable genome and the IBD signal lie. "full" is the default because the genome carries no mutation and all genetics come from exact recorded ancestry (D17): subtelomere masking exists in real data because those regions are hard to genotype and align, which a simulation with exact ancestry is not subject to, so the complete physical scaffold is the honest representation and "core" is for deliberately mimicking a masked panel. One rate for both modes leaves them directly comparable, differing only in extent, so the coordinate choice can be isolated: full gives about 17.9 Morgans of within-chromosome map, core about 16.1.

Alternatives considered. Masking the subtelomeres by default — it imports a genotyping limitation the simulator does not have. A rate per mode, each the self-consistent uniform rate that reproduces its own extent’s empirical map length — it confounds extent with recombination and leaves the two modes incomparable. The exact Pv4 core-region coordinates in place of the proxy — they are not shipped with the package, and the proxy affects only the mode that is not the default.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-params.R (only "full" and "core" are accepted, whatever the spelling); inst/validation/check_parameters.R ("core" shortens the genome); tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R ("core" and a CHROMOSOMES subset place each centromere at the same fraction of its chromosome).

D17 — The genome carries no mutation, so relatedness is identity by descent read from a forest

Decision. The mutation rate is 0 and all genetics come from the recorded genealogy. Every founder template and every import is an independent root, so the genealogy is a forest and most pairs never coalesce; tskit’s branch statistics, diversity() and divergence() among them, therefore measure no relatedness here. The package’s two measures are ibd_pairs(), where a pair’s IBD counts every stretch over which the two genomes descend from a common ancestor genome, of any age and any length, and arg_tmrca(), which gives the span-weighted mean depth over the part of the genome where a common ancestor exists, the fraction of the genome where one does, and that ancestor’s raw node time alongside. min_span does not change a pair’s IBD, and a caller who wants a recency rule writes it as a filter on the returned segments’ depth.

Why. Independent roots make a forest — about 93% of pairs never coalesce — so a statistic that scores a non-coalescing span as zero divergence is not a relatedness measure. A depth from the older of the two genomes makes one relationship give one number wherever in the run it occurred: a clonal parent-child pair reads 0 whether it arose on day 10 or day 390, while a raw node time is dominated by when the pair was sampled. Keeping the recency rule in the caller’s filter keeps the time convention visible in the analysis that chooses it rather than hidden behind an argument, and the data support no single obvious convention: about a third of segments join genomes sampled 100 or more ticks apart, and in 0.3% the older genome is itself the common ancestor, where depth from the older is 0 and depth from the younger is not.

Alternatives considered. A cutoff on the common ancestor’s absolute node time, as tskit applies one: node times run backwards from the final tick, so the cutoff is a window pinned to the end of the run, unrelated to the pair being asked about, and it erases exactly the long-dormant relapses whose ancestry is old by definition — scored that way, relapses rank below local reinfections for relatedness to earlier cases, inverting the comparison the measure exists to make. A depth argument on ibd_pairs() itself — it presumes one depth convention.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R (arg_tmrca() gives one number for one fixed relationship whatever the sampling day, and never a negative depth); tests/testthat/test-ibd.R (the segments reconstruct each pair’s IBD) and tests/testthat/test-arg.R; the ARG and IBD checks of inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R (the genealogy is a forest, relapse-to-origin IBD is exactly 1, distinct founder lineages are unrelated).

D18 — An IBD segment is a maximal stretch from one common ancestor, cut at the chromosome junctions

Decision. A segment is a maximal stretch over which two genomes descend from one common ancestor genome, cut at each chromosome junction: abutting rows with the same ancestor genome merge, a change of ancestor starts a new segment even with no gap, and min_span drops the pieces shorter than it after the cut, a piece of exactly min_span being kept. A pair gets the same segments whatever other genomes are passed, and ibd_pairs(segments = TRUE) and ibd_segments() give the same rows, each with the chromosome, both coordinate systems, the length, the common ancestor and its age. A pair’s IBD fraction counts every shared stretch, of any age and any length, so min_span does not move it (D17).

Why. A segment whose extent depends on which other genomes were asked for, or that runs across two chromosomes, cannot be compared, drawn or counted. tskit’s rows are pieces of the paths through the trees, so a pair’s ancestry splits into rows differently depending on the genomes the tree was simplified to, and a stretch continues across a junction whenever both genomes carry the same parent on both sides of it (D15). Merging on the ancestor genome rather than on its time keeps two ancestors born on one tick distinct. At min_span = 0 the merged and cut segments add up to each pair’s IBD, which ties the two views together.

Alternatives considered. Taking tskit’s rows as they come — path-dependent, and a row can run across a junction. Merging on the ancestor’s time — two ancestors born on one tick would merge. Carrying the length floor into the pair fraction — a floor applied before the cut depends on the other genomes passed, and applying it after the cut costs four to five times the time and memory.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-ibd.R: merging, cutting and flooring on a synthetic table; on a run, the same segments from any set of genomes and from both functions; no segment across a junction or below min_span; the segments adding up to each pair’s IBD; one schema for every pair; a genome with itself; pairs counted from 1.

D19 — IBD comes back as a pedigree-keyed object, and an id the tree sequence does not hold reads NA

Decision. ibd_pairs() returns a vivax_ibd object keyed by what callers hold, pedigree ids: pairs (every pair of the genomes found, a < b, zeros included), samples (each genome’s node time and the day it arose), missing, optional segments (with the common ancestor’s pedigree id and its depth), the sequence length, the floor used and the run’s end_tick. ibd_lookup() reads one pair and gives 1 for a genome with itself; as.matrix() and as.data.frame() give the table. A requested id the tree sequence does not hold warns, is listed in missing and reads NA; asking only for such ids is an error that gives the reason the run’s record holds, whether it never started or ran with RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY = FALSE, and the readers built on it then give their NA row or empty table. The Python side is one private module, called with arguments and returning arrays.

Why. An object keyed by pedigree ids needs no translation from the ids callers already have, and NA for a genome the run does not record cannot be mistaken for an unrelated pair, which a 0 can. Returning each genome’s node time is what makes a depth filter writable by the caller (D17). A module called with arguments pastes nothing into code and passes no table through a file, which costs one array conversion rather than a round trip through text.

Alternatives considered. A sparse table with implicit zeros — every reader would have to fill them in. 0 for an absent id — the confusion NA avoids. Returning the simplified tree itself — a live Python object cannot be saved, so an R object’s validity would depend on a live session, breaking saveRDS() and grid workers.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-ibd.R (the object read back; its shape on a run; lookups of relapses against their origin; segment ancestors and ages; ids not in the tree sequence; a run with no parasite) and the IBD checks of inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R.

D20 — Marker genotypes are painted on the root genomes from a panel’s allele frequencies

Decision. simulate_genotypes() takes biallelic loci as chromosome, 1-based position within that chromosome and PLAF, the ALT frequency. Each root genome — a founder template or an import (D39) — draws its allele at each locus independently, every genome carries the allele of the root genome it descends from there, and roots records that root genome for every genome and locus, the truth behind every call. Samples are clones, one genome each, or host samples grouped by sample_id (0, 1, or 0.5 where both alleles are present); error can replace a call and missing follows the errors. write_vcf() writes VCF 4.2 with one contig per simulated chromosome, haploid clone calls, unphased diploid host calls and the painting frequency as PLAF in INFO. The root genomes’ alleles are drawn for every root genome of the run before any sample is assembled.

Why. In a neutral model with no mutation (D17), painting the roots is exact: every genome descends at each position from exactly one root genome and root genomes are unrelated, so two genomes share a painted allele exactly where they share a common ancestor (D18). PLAF is what users have from a panel. Drawing for every root genome of the run first makes a genome’s alleles independent of the company it is asked for in, of the grouping into samples, and of the error and missingness laid over them.

Alternatives considered. Coalescent mutations over the recorded genealogy — a mutation never falls on a root, so no site separates two root genomes, and the frequencies would come from a coalescent prior rather than from the panel. Recapitation before mutation — the same prior, and it needs a demography the run does not provide. Painting in tskit and reading its genotype matrix — a genome alone under its root reads as missing wherever that root carries REF, and tskit’s VCF writer gives one contig in concatenated coordinates rather than one per chromosome. Drawing alleles only for the root genomes behind the genomes asked for — a genome’s alleles would depend on which others were asked for.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-genotypes.R: every genome carries its root genome’s allele, by the bookkeeping and by walking the unsimplified genealogy; root genomes are their own roots; the same root genome exactly where ibd_segments() finds a common ancestor; the root genomes and their days; the seed’s invariance; host samples; the VCF; refusals; the schema. inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R repeats four of those checks on each audit run.

Hypnozoites, relapse and the reservoir

The reservoir the model exists for: how a bite seeds hypnozoites, how they wake or die, and how relapse is counted once a relapse can hide inside an infection already there.

D21 — A bite seeds one geometric hypnozoite batch, split over the genotypes it delivers, at a fitted mean

Decision. Each genotype a bite delivers gives a blood-stage primary with probability P_PRIMARY (1 by default). Independently, the bite draws one hypnozoite batch, geometric on 0, 1, 2, … with mean ν = NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH (times NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH_BOOST from RESURGENCE_TRIGGER_TICK), and each of its hypnozoites goes to one of the delivered genotypes uniformly at random; a genotype whose share is above 0 lays down a batch that is a clone of it, as its primary is, so the two are IBD 1. A genotype can give both, either or neither, and one that seeds only hypnozoites makes no case (D29). An import draws its primary and its batch the same way (D38); founder hosts start with a blood-stage clone and no batch. The mean ships at 3, the value fitted at moderate transmission to four calibration targets, which section 13 of the model description gives with their sources; the fit counts every relapse, masked ones included (D26). ?vivax_params says the 40-host defaults are an illustrative preview, not a calibrated setting, and that the mean should be re-fitted when transmission or scale change.

Why. The batch is the one White et al. (2014) define, with mean ν per bite, and their base model treats a primary as certain given a successful inoculation, hence P_PRIMARY = 1. Drawing the batch once per bite and splitting it keeps ν that quantity and keeps co-transmission from inflating the reservoir. A default should be the value the documentation and its figures use, and the one the fit supports.

Alternatives considered. A placeholder default apart from the fitted value was considered: no documented figure uses one, and the fit does not support it.

How to check. inst/validation/calibrate_nu.R repeats the fit and checks that the shipped value sits inside all four targets; tests/testthat/test-params.R keeps the default of vivax_params() equal to the model’s own; tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R checks that an inoculation’s primary and its batch are the same genome, for bites and imports alike; inst/validation/check_parameters.R checks that a batch mean of 0 gives no relapse and that the batch boost enlarges the reservoir.

D22 — Activation and death are competing daily risks per hypnozoite, clamped so a boost stays valid

Decision. Each day a batch not in latency (D25) draws its activations, Binomial(batch_count, α), and then its deaths among the rest, Binomial(remaining, μ/(1 − α)), with α = ALPHA_ACTIVATE and μ = MU_HYPNOZOITE. Each hypnozoite thus activates with probability α and dies with probability μ that day, so its fate is settled after a geometric time with mean 1/(α + μ), and it activates rather than dies with probability α/(α + μ). From RESURGENCE_TRIGGER_TICK α is multiplied by ALPHA_ACTIVATE_BOOST; on every day the effective α is clamped at 1 − μ, and the death probability is held at 1 at most, since at α + μ = 1 the ratio can round just above it. An extreme reactivation boost therefore saturates rather than failing.

Why. The two binomials are each hypnozoite’s daily choice between activating, dying and staying, drawn for the whole batch at once, with activation and death competing as in White et al. (2014) and read as daily probabilities, as every rate in the model is (D3). The clamp keeps both probabilities valid, α below 1 and μ/(1 − α) at most 1: no more than a whole batch can activate in a day. The two rates are literature values, not fitted: α = 1/170, an average carriage of about 170 days (Mehra et al. 2024b; White et al. 2014 estimate 1/332), and μ = 1/442 (Mehra et al. 2024a, who credit White et al. 2014, whose table gives 1/425).

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R checks that the share of resolved hypnozoites that activated is α/(α + μ); tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R runs α + μ = 1, the edge of the clamp, to the end, every batch resolving on its first dormant day; tests/testthat/test-params.R accepts an activation boost of 1000, which the model clamps; inst/validation/check_parameters.R checks that an activation boost raises the relapse fraction.

D23 — One relapse per activation event, clonal to the batch it woke from

Decision. However many of a batch’s hypnozoites activate on one day, they seed one blood-stage genome, cloned from the batch, so relapse-to-origin IBD is exactly 1. The batch loses all of them; the one hypnozoite_activation row names the batch in parent1_pedigree_id and carries the count in n_hypnozoites, and one detection draw (P_DETECT_RELAPSE) and at most one course follow. Batches that wake on the same day give a relapse each, and in one host those relapses are clones of one episode (D46). Relapses therefore grow less than in proportion to the batch mean: a larger batch has more hypnozoites waking together.

Why. The hypnozoites of a batch come from one inoculation and are genetically identical, so those that wake together are one recurrent infection.

Alternatives considered. A genome for each activating hypnozoite was considered: it would over-count relapses, keep the lineage in the blood until every copy cleared, draw detection and radical cure once per hypnozoite, and weight that lineage by its count in the gametocyte pool a mosquito draws from.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-ibd.R and inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R check that every relapse has IBD 1 with its batch; the audit also checks that every activation names an established batch and that a relapse shares every root genome with it; tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R checks that a batch’s activations and deaths, counted in hypnozoites, never exceed what it held.

D24 — A hypnozoite batch empties only by activation and death

Decision. No cap clears a batch by its age: outside radical cure, by a case course (D31) or an MDA round (D35), a batch ends when activation and death have taken its last hypnozoite. MU_HYPNOZOITE must be above 0, in vivax_params() and in the model itself, so every batch ends. A batch that runs out in reproduction() has its own count set to 0 and is killed by the cleanup at the top of the same day’s early(), since killIndividuals() cannot run in reproduction(); one emptied by radical cure, which runs later in early(), goes at the next day’s cleanup and is skipped until then. The mark sits on the batch itself rather than in a global list, which avoids the Eidos scoping trap of the model’s implementation notes.

Why. White et al. (2014) give hypnozoites an exponential residence with no cap. A finite lifespan belongs in the daily death probability, not in a cutoff, which would clear whole batches at exactly the cap age and cut the long late-relapse tail the model is built to carry.

Alternatives considered. An age cap kept as a silent safety net was considered: wherever it binds it bends exactly that tail, and MU_HYPNOZOITE > 0 already ends every batch.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R, inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R and inst/validation/check_parameters.R check that no batch draws more hypnozoites than it held, which a batch left in place after running out would do; the audit also checks that the hypnozoites left unresolved equal the final reservoir in state.tsv; tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R and tests/testthat/test-slim.R refuse MU_HYPNOZOITE = 0.

D25 — Latent hypnozoites die, and a batch moves through latency as one unit

Decision. With K_LATENCY = k above 0, every new batch starts k latency stages away from activation. Each latent day it first loses Binomial(batch_count, μ) hypnozoites, logged as hypnozoite_clearance like any other death, and then, if any are left, moves on one stage with probability δ = DELTA_LATENCY; it cannot activate while latent, nor on the day it leaves latency. A hypnozoite therefore relapses with probability [δ(1 − μ)/(1 − (1 − δ)(1 − μ))]^k × α/(α + μ), 0.480 at k = 2 and the shipped rates against 0.722 without latency, and because survival favours the batches that move through quickly, one that leaves latency alive has been latent k/(1 − (1 − δ)(1 − μ)) days on average (163 at k = 2), not k/δ. DELTA_LATENCY must lie in (0, 1] when K_LATENCY is above 0.

Why. It is the model the documentation cites: White et al. (2014) apply death in every latent compartment and track latency per infection, which is why the batch moves as one unit. At DELTA_LATENCY = 0 a temperate batch could never leave latency, and so could never relapse.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R imports 300 infections at K_LATENCY = 2, with no onward transmission, runs until every batch has resolved, and checks the share of hypnozoites that activated against the formula above; it also checks that latent deaths in imported batches carry is_imported = 1. tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R refuses DELTA_LATENCY = 0 at K_LATENCY = 1, and inst/validation/check_parameters.R checks that temperate latency delays each batch’s first relapse.

D26 — A relapse into a patent clone of its own lineage is counted like any other, and flagged

Decision. A relapse can begin while a patent clone of its own lineage is in the host, most often the primary of the same bite or an earlier relapse of the same batch; at the shipped defaults about 80% of relapses do. Such a relapse is a new genome, counted as a relapse and drawn for detection like any other, so it can be reported and treated. Its hypnozoite_activation row has into_patent_lineage = 1 (0 on other activations, -1 on every other row), and exclude_masked = TRUE leaves these masked relapses out of classify_cases(), relapse_fraction(), force_of_infection(), recurrences() and summarise_run(), and passes over them in time_to_relapse() (D27). The activation runs in reproduction() and sees only clones born on earlier days (one that ends that day counts), so a relapse that starts on the same day as another clone of its lineage, from another batch waking, a recrudescence or a bite, is not flagged for that clone: two batches of one lineage that wake together, with no earlier clone of it in the host, are both 0.

Why. A study that genotypes the host would see only the infection already there, not a recurrence, while hypnozoites did wake and the model’s observation layer can report the relapse; which count an analysis needs depends on its question, and the flag gives it both.

Alternatives considered. Merging such an activation into the clone already there was considered: it would build one reading into the model.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R rebuilds each host’s patent clones from events.tsv in a run with treatment failures, recrudescence and an MDA round, and the flag matches on every activation; tests/testthat/test-episodes.R checks that exclude_masked removes exactly the flagged activations, and tests/testthat/test-summary.R that it leaves them out of every relapse column of summarise_run() and changes no other column.

D27 — Time to first relapse is measured per hypnozoite batch

Decision. time_to_relapse() gives one row per hypnozoite batch, timed from the day it is laid down (for an import that also brings a blood-stage infection, the day after it) to its first relapse, which the activation’s parent1_pedigree_id ties to the batch. A batch with no relapse is censored on the day its last hypnozoite leaves it, by death or radical cure (emptied = "censor", the default), or at SIM_DAYS; emptied = "follow" follows an emptied batch to SIM_DAYS, the curve a trial reports, where radical cure shows as relapses prevented. With exclude_masked = TRUE the clock stops at the first relapse a study could see as a recurrence, although a masked relapse’s hypnozoites still leave the batch. plot_relapse_km() draws the Kaplan–Meier fraction of batches not yet relapsed.

Why. A relapse comes from a batch, and the time from the infection that laid a batch down to its first relapse is the quantity cohort and trial data report; censoring at emptying gives the time to relapse of the hypnozoites that live.

Alternatives considered. A clock per host was considered: a host’s first relapse can come from the batch of a later bite, which mixes the wait for reinfection into the measure, and since founders carry no batch, a clock started at founder seeding makes the curve’s shape depend on how many hosts are founders.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-relapse-metrics.R: a fixture’s five batches, censored, followed and with a masked relapse passed over; the curve’s steps; a run with no batch; on an import cohort, every batch timed from its establishment, and the batches radical cure reached first ending as emptied; a batch emptied in a run that goes extinct; every liver-stage row that names a genome takes hypnozoites out of its batch. inst/validation/check_parameters.R checks that temperate latency delays each batch’s first relapse.

D28 — The relapse rate is per person-year at risk, and the relapse fraction has two readings

Decision. summarise_run() (D50) gives the relapse rate as relapses_per_py_at_risk: every relapse in its window over person_years_at_risk, the person-time of the hosts ever infected. A host’s time starts the day after its first establishment, a primary or a hypnozoite batch from a bite or an import, and runs to the window’s end, also after an extinction; founder seeding does not put a host at risk. The relapse fraction has two readings, both counted per clone onset and both including each host’s first case: relapse_frac_acquisitions, relapses over imported, local reinfection and relapse cases, the unit of the relapse-fraction target in section 13 of the model description, and relapse_frac_episodes, relapses over every case, recrudescence included. relapse_fraction() and summarise_run() give both, each NA when its denominator is 0, and the two are equal on a run with no recrudescence, as at the defaults. Masked relapses (D26) are counted unless exclude_masked = TRUE; ?relapse_fraction says the batch mean is fitted with every relapse counted, and what leaving the masked ones out gives.

Why. A host never infected cannot relapse, while one whose first infection left only a batch can, and the run’s length, not its last event, is the period observed. A recrudescence is a new episode but not a newly acquired parasite (D33), so once recrudescence is on both readings are needed, and names that say their unit keep them from being swapped. A fraction with nothing to divide is not 0.

Alternatives considered. Dividing by the person-time of every host was considered: it counts hosts never at risk, so the rate falls with the share never bitten. Counting every ever-infected host over the window’s whole length was considered too: it counts a host’s days before its first infection.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-relapse-metrics.R: both fractions, with and without the masked relapse, and a run with no case. tests/testthat/test-summary.R: a fixture’s relapses and person-time, with and without a window, and a run with no infection; on a run, every activation counted and person-time to SIM_DAYS after an extinction; summarise_run()’s columns against relapse_fraction() and the person-time over several windows, and exclude_masked in every relapse column. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: on a run with recrudescence, each reading equals the share of relapses among its cases, and the acquisitions reading is the larger.

Detection, treatment, recrudescence and MDA

The observation layer and the drugs: what a surveillance system sees, what a course does to a host and its reservoir, what survives one, and what a mass round reaches that a case course cannot.

D29 — Detection is drawn once per bite, import, relapse or recrudescence, and an infection with no blood stage is no case

Decision. Whether a case is reported is drawn once per bite, for every genotype the bite delivers, at P_DETECT_PRIMARY; once per import, at P_DETECT_PRIMARY too; once per activation, which makes one relapse (D23), at P_DETECT_RELAPSE; and once per recrudescence, at P_DETECT_RECRUD. The outcome is the detected flag on the case’s onset rows. A detected case can be prescribed a course (D30, D31), and the reported cases, detected == 1 in classify_cases() and force_of_infection(detected_only = TRUE), are the observed line list; the true one holds every case. A bite or an import that establishes only a hypnozoite batch, which P_PRIMARY below 1 allows, makes no blood stage, so it is no case: no row of it carries a detection flag, and it gets no course. Detection depends on origin only through the three probabilities, so active and passive surveillance cannot be told apart.

Why. The genotypes one bite delivers are separate cases of one episode (D46), but one person presents with them, so they are reported and treated together, never for one genotype and not the other. Detection differs by origin because relapses are often subpatent, so a realistic P_DETECT_RELAPSE is much lower than a primary’s (0.15, say), and Ross et al. (2025) put recurrence detectability at 0.13–0.49 of a primary’s, so P_DETECT_RECRUD should usually sit well below P_DETECT_PRIMARY. A batch in the liver cannot have caused symptoms, and a course given for it would clear the host’s other clones and, with radical cure, the batch the same bite had just seeded.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: at P_PRIMARY = 0, with full coverage and undetected relapses, no course is given. tests/testthat/test-load.R and inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R: the detection flag is set only on the blood-stage onset rows of bites, imports, relapses and recrudescences, never on founder seeding or a batch. inst/validation/check_parameters.R: lower detection probabilities thin the observed line list, and at the defaults every case is reported. tests/testthat/test-windows.R: force_of_infection(detected_only = TRUE) counts the reported cases.

D30 — Case management has its own window, separate from vector control

Decision. TREATMENT_START and TREATMENT_END bound case management: a case detected on days TREATMENT_START to TREATMENT_END - 1 can be prescribed a course. They default to the whole run, so a coverage alone is the switch: set BLOODCURE_COVERAGE and detected cases are treated. One helper, caseManagementOn(), gates every case-based course; it is asked in decideTreatment(), which every case goes through. INTERVENTION_* is vector control and scales biting only (D37): it does not touch treatment, and the treatment window does not touch biting. The window gates the decision, not the delivery, so a case detected on the programme’s last day completes its course after the window closes. A coverage set against a window that holds no day of the run, one that is closed, ends by day 1 or opens after the run ends, is refused, by validate_params() and by the model itself (D43).

Why. Case management is drugs given to diagnosed patients and vector control is bed nets and spraying; nothing should make one imply the other, and a scenario can treat cases without changing biting. Expressing the gate once keeps the sites where cases arise from drifting apart. A patient who presents on the programme’s last day is not refused treatment. A coverage against a closed window would silently give no treatment at all.

Alternatives considered. One window for both programmes, with a warning when a coverage is set without it: it keeps a coupling that has no modelling reason, and forces a change in biting on anyone who wants treatment. A treatment efficacy of its own within the shared window: the timing of the two programmes would stay tied.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: a coverage alone gives courses; a bounded window gives courses only from its first day, with a short tail after it closes; and a coverage against a closed window is refused. The window test asserts when courses come rather than how many, because a window open throughout a run can give fewer courses than a late one, by preventing the cases it would treat. tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R: opening the vector-control window alone gives none. tests/testthat/test-slim.R: a run started directly with SLiM refuses a coverage against a closed window too.

D31 — Treatment is decided where the case arises and applied to the host later; radical cure is nested inside it

Decision. decideTreatment() runs where a detected case arises, at a bite, an import, a relapse or a recrudescence. Inside the treatment window (D30), and when the host has no course pending, it draws a blood-stage course at BLOODCURE_COVERAGE and, nested inside it, radical cure at RADCURE_COVERAGE, and schedules the course (D32). applyTreatment() gives the course in early() on the day it lands, before the day’s natural clearance, to the host rather than to one lineage: every patent blood-stage clone the host carries, except one patent only since that day (D32), clears unless it survives, at P_BLOODCURE_SURVIVAL (D33), and radical cure, if drawn, acts on every hypnozoite batch the host carries. Radical cure is liver-stage only and never clears the current blood stage, and RADCURE_COVERAGE is the probability of radical cure given a course, not a coverage of its own. Its efficacy is per person by default (RADCURE_MODE = "person"): one all-or-nothing draw, in which the whole reservoir survives with probability P_RAD_SURVIVAL (0.29, about 71% cure). RADCURE_MODE = "hypnozoite" draws each hypnozoite’s survival independently, so a course can clear part of a reservoir; there P_RAD_SURVIVAL is a per-hypnozoite probability, and the same number is not the same efficacy. A host takes one course at a time: a second case while a course is pending schedules none, and a treated case stays infectious until the drugs land.

Why. early() is the first point at which the genomes made in reproduction() are visible, so a course applied there reaches the batch seeded by the infection behind the case, an import’s included, whose batch is cloned the day after it arrives (D38). Drugs clear the blood-stage parasites in a person, not one clone, so the course treats the patient, and a detected relapse gets a schizonticide like any other case. Radical cure is the 8-aminoquinoline class (primaquine, tafenoquine), the one lever on the dormant liver reservoir and a class apart from the blood schizonticides; primaquine is not given without a schizonticide, hence the nesting. Per-person efficacy is how clinical efficacy is reported, as recurrence prevented per patient, and 0.29 sits near the 70% effectiveness White et al. (2018) assume for a 14-day primaquine course, given poor adherence. The per-hypnozoite mode is the only one in which some of a host’s genotypes survive radical cure, which is what reshapes relapse diversity after treatment.

Alternatives considered. A treatment flag on the new lineage, set where the case arises: it treats one clone rather than the patient, and cannot reach the batch the same bite seeds, which SLiM keeps out of sight until reproduction() ends. Per-person efficacy alone: it cannot clear part of a reservoir, so the per-hypnozoite mode is offered beside it.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: a blood-stage coverage alone gives courses, radical cure nested in them clears hypnozoites, and with RADCURE_COVERAGE = 0 none is cleared. tests/testthat/test-relapse-metrics.R: on a cohort of imports, a case’s radical cure empties the batch its own import seeded before any of it activates; in the per-hypnozoite mode, case and MDA radical cure take hypnozoites out of the batches they name. inst/validation/check_parameters.R: radical cure shrinks the reservoir, a weaker one leaves a bigger reservoir, and blood-stage treatment lowers prevalence.

D32 — A course lands at least a day after its case, and the treatment and recrudescence delays follow the 1/D rule

Decision. A course is scheduled 1 + rgeom(1, 1/TREATMENT_DELAY) days after its case: each day after the case it arrives with probability 1/TREATMENT_DELAY, so the delay is at least one day and its mean is exactly TREATMENT_DELAY, 7 by default. On the day it lands, a case course passes over any clone whose blood stage began that day. TREATMENT_DELAY is at least 1, where 1 means the next day, the fastest response the model can represent. The delay from suppression to recrudescence, MEAN_RECRUD_DELAY, follows the same rule under its default shape (D34). Both parameters are finite, from 1 to 10^6 days; validate_params() and the model itself (D43) refuse other values.

Why. A clone that became patent today cannot yet have caused symptoms, prompted care-seeking or been diagnosed, and natural clearance follows the same rule: a clone cannot clear on the day its blood stage began. The rule is needed at both ends. At the decision, because a course landing on the day of its case would pass over the clone behind the case and be spent all the same, leaving the patient untreated; at the application, because a course given for one case must not reach a different clone that appeared on its landing day. Under the 1/D rule every duration parameter means what it says (D3). MDA waits for no symptoms, so a round is exempt from the application rule (D35).

Alternatives considered. A geometric draw of mean TREATMENT_DELAY that can return 0, floored at one day: the zeros pile onto the first day, so the mean exceeds the parameter, 7.125 days for 7. Accepting TREATMENT_DELAY = 0 as another name for the next day: two values for one behaviour, where 1 already means the next day.
