How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: with a pulse of detected imports as the only cases, at a delay of 1 every course and every recrudescence comes the next day, and at 4 both delays have mean 4 with a quarter of them one day long, a share that any mass at zero would inflate. tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R: values below 1, infinite or above 10^6 are refused. tests/testthat/test-slim.R: a run started directly with SLiM refuses values below 1 or infinite.

D33 — A recrudescence mints a new genome clonal to its holder, and is a case but not an acquisition

Decision. A clone that survives a course carries on at full density (bloodcure_persist) or, with probability P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL, is suppressed below patency (bloodcure_subpatent, which ends its patent span). A suppressed clone, a holder, is not patent: it is out of moi_active (state.tsv counts it in moi_subpatent), cannot be detected, and no later case course reaches it. It is present, counting toward MAX_MOI, and transmissible: the bite loop asks whether a host is infectious, not whether it is patent, and a holder joins the gametocyte pool a feeding mosquito draws from with probability SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY, 0.15 by default. A holder does not clear naturally. After its delay (D34) it re-expands as a recrudescence: a new genome cloned from the holder in reproduction(), with a pedigree id of its own and its own place in the tree sequence, dated at the recurrence, while the holder itself is removed in that day’s early(), before the courses and clearance. The new genome carries the holder’s lineage, and its row gives -1 for inoculation_id and oocyst_id and names the holder in parent1_pedigree_id. A recrudescence is a case, detected at P_DETECT_RECRUD and treated like any other (D29, D31), and the fourth origin of classify_cases(), so it counts in case counts, incidence and host timelines. It is not an acquisition (is_acquisition = FALSE), so FOI leaves it out, and the metrics that have both readings, molFOB, the relapse fraction and Rc, report both, by unit (D28, D50, D53). P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL defaults to 0, so a default run has no recrudescence.

Why. A recurrence has three causes, relapse, reinfection and recrudescence (Taylor et al. 2019), and the model represents all three. Minting gives every case a genome of its own: the recurrence’s genome is dated at the recurrence rather than at the original inoculation, and its IBD of 1 to the earlier episode is a measurement between two genomes, not a genome paired with itself. Because the new genome inherits the lineage, removing the holder and adding it leaves MOI, prevalence, COI and the reservoir exactly as they are. Patency, infectiousness and presence are counted apart because a holder separates them: counted as patent it would make an episode no one can see, and a patent count in the bite loop would silently block the transmission SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY permits. The mosquito-feeding studies Koepfli et al. (2021) compile put submicroscopic carriers at 0.10–0.20 of the infectivity of microscopy-positive ones, so neither 0 nor 1 is defensible. With natural clearance off while subpatent, every holder recrudesces unless an MDA round clears it (D35), so without MDA P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL is exactly P(recrudescence | the course failed), comparable with the failure rate of a therapeutic-efficacy study. No new parasite enters the host, so a recrudescence is no acquisition; a field molFOB, which compares genotypes between visits, often counts it as a new clone, because the clone is undetectable at the earlier visit, and the gap between the two readings estimates that bias. Its ids are -1 because a recrudescence is no bite, and inherited ones would put it in another case’s co-transmission group. The default of 0 matches recrudescence at 0.2–0.3% of recurrences after chloroquine or artesunate (Taylor et al. 2019, n = 1441); the state matters in a chloroquine-resistant setting.

Alternatives considered. Reusing the holder’s individual: two onsets would share one pedigree id, against the rule that creation events mint unique ids, and the recurrence’s onward transmission could not be told from the earlier infection’s. Re-dating the holder’s node at the recurrence: a node keeps the time its genome is made. Minting without removing the holder: one failed course would recrudesce again and again.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: at P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL = 0 nothing is suppressed; at 1 every failure suppresses, and each recrudescence has an id of its own, a holder as its parent, -1 ids and a later day than its suppression, is a case of its own origin and no acquisition, and nothing clears twice; a recrudescence is IBD 1 to its holder at a TMRCA of 0, in the holder’s lineage. inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R, on its configuration with recrudescence: creation events mint unique pedigree ids, every clearance matches an onset, and none repeats. tests/testthat/test-run.R: a holder counts toward MAX_MOI even at SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY = 0.

D34 — The recrudescence delay is geometric with a mean of 10.5 days, selectable, and a literature assumption

Decision. Each day after its suppression a holder re-expands with probability 1/MEAN_RECRUD_DELAY, so the delay is at least one day with that mean, 10.5 days by default: a median of 7 days, and about 94% within day 28. RECRUD_DELAY_DIST sets the shape: "geometric", the default; "poisson", 1 + Poisson(D − 1) with mean D, a tight-window sensitivity arm; or "fixed", round(D) days with halves rounded up, 11 at 10.5. Every shape is at least one day. 10.5 days is a literature assumption, pending parameterisation, which the roadmap lists for sensitivity analysis.

Why. The only published fit for this quantity models the time to recrudescence as exponential (Taylor et al. 2019), and the ceiling of an exponential delay on a day scale is a geometric one. Every other duration in the model is geometric too (D3). 10.5 days is the reciprocal of their posterior median rate, 0.095 a day, but they hold the rate with a strongly informative Gamma(100, 1000) prior, mean 0.1 a day, for identifiability, and the posterior barely moves from it, so the value is close to the prior rather than an estimate from data. At this mean nearly all recrudescences fall within the standard 28-day follow-up of a therapeutic-efficacy study, where a study can see them.

Alternatives considered. A Poisson delay as the default: no source supports it, and its spread, a standard deviation of about 3 days at this mean, is too narrow for regrowth from an unobserved density; it is offered as the "poisson" arm, a tight-window contrast. A gamma delay with a shape parameter: regrowth is log-linear, so the delay is a logarithm of the surviving biomass, which argues for a peaked delay with a floor; but it needs a second parameter, and the family with a published fit behind it is the default.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: at a mean of 1 every shape gives a one-day delay, and at 4 the geometric delay has mean 4 with a quarter of delays one day long. tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R: a mean below 1, infinite or above 10^6 days, and a shape outside the three, are refused. tests/testthat/test-slim.R: a run started directly with SLiM refuses a mean below 1 or infinite, and runs each shape.

D35 — MDA is one round of the same course, drawn per host, and reaches the clones a case course cannot

Decision. MDA_TICK gives one round of mass drug administration through the same applyTreatment() as case management: blood-stage drugs and radical cure for every host it reaches, those carrying only hypnozoites included, at the efficacies P_BLOODCURE_SURVIVAL, P_RAD_SURVIVAL and RADCURE_MODE set. RADCURE_COVERAGE, a probability given a case course, plays no part in it. The round reaches each host with probability MDA_COVERAGE, drawn only when the coverage is below 1, so a round that reaches everyone draws no number. Only hosts not empty at the round are drawn; the draw does not depend on infection, so the coverage is that of the whole population, and mda_bloodcure_given and mda_radcure_given count the courses to those hosts. The round comes in early(), after the day’s natural clearance and before its imports, and the treatment window does not gate it. Because it waits for no symptoms, it reaches two kinds of clone a case course does not: a clone that became patent earlier the same day, and a holder (D33), which it clears with probability 1 − P_BLOODCURE_SURVIVAL, cancelling its recrudescence. A cleared holder is logged as mda_subpatent_clear, which ends no episode, since its patent span ends at its suppression; a holder that survives keeps its schedule and is not suppressed again. A patent clone that survives the round persists or is suppressed as under a case course. MDA_TICK = 1 is refused when a founder host carries a copy of another founder’s genome (D40): a day-1 round could clear the template before the copy is made.

Why. One course for both paths means the two cannot diverge. Coverage is the whole policy question for MDA, what separates a feasible campaign from an idealised one; without it an imperfect campaign could only be mimicked through efficacy, which confounds the two. Neither filter a case course keeps has its reason under MDA, which is given to everyone, symptoms or not: the one-day rule stands for the delay from patency to symptoms and care (D32), and the holder rule for a course prescribed for a case other than the holder’s. Drugs taken on the day a clone reaches the blood act on it too.

Alternatives considered. A round blind to holders: it would leave the very reservoir it exists to clear. Drawing a surviving holder’s suppression again: it would reset the holder’s schedule and log a second end to a patent span that has already ended.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-treatment.R: at a round, each holder is cleared (mda_subpatent_clear, never to recrudesce) or left on its schedule with no row that day, a clone the round has just suppressed is not drawn again, and nothing clears twice; with P_BLOODCURE_SURVIVAL = 0, a day-2 round clears every founder copy seeded that morning and leaves no blood-stage clone, and the host trajectory plot draws such a one-day clone. tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-slim.R: MDA_TICK = 1 is refused only when a founder host carries a copy. tests/testthat/test-relapse-metrics.R: in the per-hypnozoite mode, a round’s radical cure takes hypnozoites out of the batches it names.

Seasonality, vector control and importation

What comes from outside and what scales it: the season, local vector control, the three import routes, and the two ways a case can be called imported.

D36 — The seasonal factor peaks on the day its parameter names, and scales biting and the Poisson import rate

Decision. On day t of the run a mosquito bites with probability BITING_RATE × max(0, 1 + SEASONAL_AMP cos(2π(t − SEASONAL_PHASE)/365)), times the vector-control factor inside its window (D37) and BITING_RATE_BOOST from the resurgence trigger. The cosine puts the maximum exactly on day SEASONAL_PHASE, and at every 365 days from it, so the parameter is what its table says it is: the day of the year of the peak. SEASONAL_AMP is at least 0, since a negative amplitude would put a trough on that day (a trough on day x is SEASONAL_PHASE = x + 182.5); above 1, the factor is 0 for part of each year, a legitimate edge value that runs (D42). The same factor multiplies the Poisson import rate, IMPORT_RATE_PER_TICK; the pulse and the daily count take none (D37).

Why. A parameter should mean what it says. With a sine in place of the cosine the peak would fall about 91 days, a quarter of a year, after SEASONAL_PHASE, and anyone setting it to a real transmission-season day would be a quarter of a year out. The import rate follows the season because travel, or transmission where the travellers pick up their infections, can follow the same season as local biting.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-params.R and tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R: vivax_params(), which works the factor out as the model does, puts the import-rate and biting peaks on SEASONAL_PHASE (day 100 at SEASONAL_PHASE = 100, and day 3020, eight years on, once a boost starts on day 3000), and refuses a negative SEASONAL_AMP, as the model does in a run started directly (tests/testthat/test-slim.R); tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R: an amplitude of 1.5 runs to its last day.

D37 — Vector control scales biting only

Decision. On days INTERVENTION_START to INTERVENTION_END − 1 the daily biting probability is multiplied by 1 − INTERVENTION_EFFICACY, together with the seasonal factor and the resurgence boost (D36), and the factor scales nothing else: not importation, and not treatment, which has its own window, TREATMENT_START/TREATMENT_END (D30). The Poisson import rate takes the seasonal factor and IMPORT_RATE_BOOST from RESURGENCE_TRIGGER_TICK; the pulse (N_IMPORTS) and the daily count (N_IMPORTS_PER_TICK) take no factor. A border measure is IMPORT_RATE_BOOST, which at 0 closes the border from the trigger, or the import window itself. vivax_params() works out the import rate’s peak for its warning (D40) with the same factors.

Why. Imports are infections acquired elsewhere, which local bed nets and spraying do not reach; what limits them is a border measure, which the boost and the window express.

Alternatives considered. Scaling the Poisson import rate by the vector-control factor would tie a border measure to local vector control, so an arm with vector control and open borders could not be expressed at all. Scaling the pulse and the daily count by the season or the boost as well: they are values the user sets directly, and a user who wants them to vary can vary them.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R: under full vector control from day 10 no bite or uptake happens from day 10 while imports keep arriving, opening the window gives no course, and IMPORT_RATE_BOOST = 0 from the trigger stops the imports; tests/testthat/test-params.R: an import rate of 40 a day into 30 hosts warns at its full value under 90% vector control; inst/validation/check_parameters.R: vector control lowers prevalence.

D38 — An import is minted in a scratch subpopulation in early(), and its second compartment is cloned the next day

Decision. Imports arrive in early(). Each import’s outcomes, the same as a bite’s, are rolled before any genome exists: a blood-stage primary with probability P_PRIMARY and a hypnozoite batch of geometric size with a bite’s mean; an import that takes in neither is logged as vh_inoculation_import_no_take and mints nothing. The day’s imports that take are minted together in one scratch subpopulation with addSubpop(), moved into their hosts with takeMigrants(), and the scratch subpopulation is removed in the same callback. The migrated genome becomes whichever compartment the import made, so an import that makes only hypnozoites arrives as its batch and is no case (D29). An import that takes in both queues its batch, which the next day’s reproduction() clones from the primary and logs under the same inoculation_id. Both rows log parent1_pedigree_id as -1, while the tree sequence records the primary as the batch’s parent. An imported case is detected and decided for treatment on arrival like any other (D31), and its course lands no earlier than the next day’s early() (D32), after the batch is cloned, so a radical cure given for it reaches that batch. In the tree sequence the migrated genome’s node keeps the scratch subpopulation as its population, so a node’s population does not name an import’s host; nothing in the package reads node populations.

Why. SLiM calls reproduction() once for each existing individual, so with no parasite alive it never runs: an import seeded there could never reach an empty parasite population or re-seed a run that reached elimination. Outside reproduction(), addSubpop() is the only way to mint a genome, the idiom that also mints the founder lineages on day 1, and takeMigrants() keeps the pedigree id, the tag and every stored value. SLiM refuses to clone a genome minted the same day, and two genomes minted by addSubpop() are unrelated roots, so a clone on the next day is the only way to make an import’s batch IBD 1 to its primary: one inoculation delivers one sporozoite population, and a relapse of an imported infection is then clonal to the infection that caused it, as a local relapse is. Rolling the outcomes first leaves no genome with nowhere to go. The logged parent stays -1 because nothing inside the simulation is an import’s parent, and inoculation_id and lineage_id already say that the two rows are one inoculation; logging the primary as the batch’s parent would let anyone reconstructing transmission from the event log infer a blood-to-liver transmission within the host that never happened.

Alternatives considered. A permanent sentinel individual that keeps reproduction() running in an empty population: alive at the end of every run, it would be a tree-sequence sample with a pedigree id in every all-samples analysis, and would need guards through the model’s busiest callback. A transient inoculum genome cloned into both compartments, which would give an import the sibling topology of a local bite: it costs a one-day delay on every imported blood-stage infection and an extra individual, for a topology that a structured source population (D39) gives as a by-product.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R: an inoculation’s primary and its batch are IBD 1 in the tree sequence, imports included; inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R: each inoculation_id is one host, a local inoculation’s rows share a day, and an import’s span at most one; tests/testthat/test-run.R, among others, runs founder-free populations seeded only by imports.

D39 — Imported genotypes are unrelated founders

Decision. Every import enters as a root of the genealogy, with no ancestry: the limit of an infinitely large, infinitely diverse source population, in which no two imports are related and no import is related to the parasites it joins. simulate_genotypes() paints each import, as it paints each founder template, independently from the same allele frequencies (D20), so an import’s genotype differs from local ones through its genealogy, never through differentiated allele frequencies.

Why. Unrelated founders add no parameter to the model, while a structured source would add the source’s diversity as a calibration axis and change what an import is. The cost is stated rather than left implicit: imports are maximally distinguishable by construction, so any result on how identifiable imported cases are is an upper bound, conditional on this assumption. The README’s limitations and sections 8, 11 and 15 of the model description say so.

Alternatives considered. A structured source deme with migration, the population-genetics convention for immigration, under which imported genomes carry real ancestry and coalesce with one another in the source: a planned extension (the roadmap). Under it an import’s inoculum would be a real genome, so its two compartments would be siblings cloned from it, as a local bite’s are, in place of the primary-to-batch clone of D38.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-genotypes.R: the root genomes are the founder templates and the imports, and distinct root genomes share no IBD segment.

D40 — Imports land in uniformly random hosts under the bite’s gate, at most one a host a day

Decision. A day’s imports go to distinct hosts drawn uniformly at random, as bites do, so an import can land in a host that already carries a clone. Each meets the same gate a bite does, counting the clones the host gained earlier that day (D10); a refused import is logged as vh_inoculation_import_no_take. A host takes at most one import a day, so a day’s imports beyond N_HOSTS are dropped, and vivax_params() warns when N_IMPORTS, N_IMPORTS_PER_TICK or the two together would bring more than N_HOSTS on a day of the run, or when the Poisson rate at its seasonal and boosted peak, with the daily count, would draw more than N_HOSTS on a day with probability above 0.01. A pulse on day 1 lands like a pulse on any other day, alongside the founders, with one difference: a founder host carrying a copy of another founder’s genome (N_FOUNDER_LINEAGES < N_FOUNDER_HOSTS) receives the copy on day 2, so on day 1 it is still empty, takes an import even at MAX_MOI = 1, and from day 2 carries both. A naive population is N_FOUNDER_HOSTS = 0 with an import path inside the run.

Why. Random placement makes an import as likely as a bite to share its host with a local clone, which is the setting a study detecting or classifying imported cases faces. One import a host a day keeps the largest import rate the parameters allow, 1e6 a day, cheap to run, and the warning makes the dropped excess visible. A day-1 pulse keeps the founders because the parameters ask for them; a naive population is expressible directly.

Alternatives considered. Filling a day’s imports from hosts without a blood-stage infection first: an import would almost never meet a local clone, which makes imports easier to detect and classify than random placement does. Placing every import with replacement: at the cap of 1e6 imports a day, each of the default 40 hosts would take about 25,000 a day. Reading a day-1 pulse as a naive population: it would silently drop the founders the parameters ask for.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-run.R: 100 imports into 200 hosts, half of them founders, put about half into founder hosts; at MAX_MOI = 1 none lands in a founder host still carrying its clone, and the refusals are logged; a pulse of 50 into 30 hosts brings exactly 30, one a host, with the warning; a day-1 pulse keeps the founders. tests/testthat/test-params.R: MAX_MOI = 0 is refused, as it is in a run started directly (tests/testthat/test-slim.R), and a day’s counts above N_HOSTS, or a rate that often draws more, warn.

D41 — An import class comes from the true chain, and a travel rule is scored against it

Decision. classify_chain() gives every case, a row of classify_cases(), its generation: the fewest transmission links from a clone acquired by importation, through both routes (D52), found breadth first from every import at once. A recrudescence counts as the clone it came from, and of an outcrossed oocyst’s two parents the shorter chain counts. The class follows the WHO malaria terminology (World Health Organization, 2021): imported (generation 0: an import, a relapse of an import’s batch, or a recrudescence of either), introduced (1), indigenous (from an import) (2 or more) and indigenous (local lineage) (no import in the chain); import_pedigree_id names the import row the chain starts from, the batch for an imported relapse and the smaller id on a tie. classify_travel() answers the other question, what a rule that knows only travel history concludes: a case is imported (recent travel) when its host received an import that established, as a blood stage or as hypnozoites only, on one of the window days that end on the case’s day (60 by default), and local (no recent travel) otherwise. Each import is one trip, on the day it arrived, although an import that takes in both compartments logs its batch the next day (D38); an import that established nothing is no trip.

Why. The true class is what a travel rule, or a genetic classifier, is scored against. A surveillance system records the journey, not which compartment the parasite ended in, so a traveller who brings back only hypnozoites has travelled. The look-back decides most of the result, and for vivax no window is right: a hypnozoite can wake many months after the trip, so a short window misses many imported relapses, while one long enough to catch a hypnozoite that activates a year after the trip also flags what its host acquires locally in that year; that disagreement is the quantity classify_travel() exists to measure, what a travel rule costs, not a defect of it.

Alternatives considered. Walking each case’s parents back one case at a time gives the same classes, more slowly, and loses the chain at a recrudescence unless the walk takes it back to its clone. Counting only the imports that established a blood stage as trips confuses the traveller with the infection. Counting an import that established nothing as a trip: the model’s only travel is the import of a parasite, and travellers who bring none back are not modelled, so it would add a few of them and leave out the rest.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-imports.R: a fixture’s classes, generations and import rows, with an imported relapse traced from its batch and an import’s recrudescence; on a run, the imported class is exactly the imported cases and each generation is one link from the one before; the travel window’s bounds, one trip per import on its arrival day, a hypnozoite-only import counted and one that established nothing not; tests/testthat/test-example-run.R: the example run holds all four classes.

Parameters, outputs and the R interface

The surface a user meets: what is refused and what runs, how a run’s tables read the same way every time, the truth tables built from the event log, and the one function per question that reads them.

D42 — Values the model cannot run are refused before SLiM starts; legitimate edge values run to the end

Decision. validate_params() refuses, before SLiM starts and with a message that names the parameter, every value the model cannot run or would run as something else: a value that is missing, not a single value, or of another kind than its default (a number, TRUE/FALSE or a string), or a number with a class, such as a bit64::integer64 or a lubridate duration; a count, SIM_DAYS, a scheduling day or a fixed delay that is not whole; a value outside the bounds that ?vivax_params and section 10 of the model description give it, such as a probability outside [0, 1], a mean duration below one day or a negative count; a number that is not finite, or not 0 and below 1e-300 in size; text that is not UTF-8 or holds control characters; a CHROMOSOMES that is unreadable, names a chromosome outside 1 to 14 or twice, or runs a range high-low; and a value above one of the sizes capped far above anything realistic, which ?vivax_params and section 10 of the model description give with each parameter. A run that reaches day 99999, the day the defaults use for never, must move those days past its end. A set in which no parasite can ever arise, such as one with no founder and no import on a day of the run, and a coverage set against a closed treatment window (D30) are refused too. The legitimate edges run at their natural limit instead: no imports at a rate of 0, a one-day delay at the minimum, a hypnozoite’s death probability capped at 1 when activation and death together reach 1, no infectiousness for a host without a blood stage, a zero batch from a mean of 0, a zero oocyst count from a gamma draw that underflows to 0, and an exact draw, by inversion, of the oocyst count of an uptake whose 10,000 gamma-Poisson tries all find none; a founder-free run whose imports never take ends cleanly as never started (D5). Spellings that mean the same value, such as a named number, a value in I(), a whole number carrying floating-point noise (1.1 * 100), a number or a factor from expand.grid() for a text parameter, text in another encoding, or spaces around the commas and dashes of CHROMOSOMES, are stored in the form SLiM is given (D7). The model makes the same checks for a run started without R (D43).

Why. A sweep must not lose cells to engine errors, and a refusal that names the parameter beats a stack trace from tick 200; each refused value would otherwise stop the run part-way or run it as something else: a string P_TRANS_VH is compared as text, 12.5 founder hosts seed 13, and a lubridate duration counts seconds. SLiM, and the provenance it writes into the tree sequence, need UTF-8 text, and SLiM’s command line cannot read a number between 0 and about 2.2e-308. A set in which no parasite can arise would end with an empty event log, which in a sweep cannot be told from a cell that saw no transmission. The caps sit far above any realistic setting and well below where SLiM’s draws fail: binomial sizes are 32-bit, Poisson draws wrap above 2^32 and the geometric delay saturates near 4e9 days. The oocyst cap is on the mean count per uptake rather than on LAMBDA_OOCYSTS, since a small K_OOCYSTS gives a tail whose mean is many times lambda; at K_OOCYSTS = 0.001 the count already comes within 0.5% of the largest variance a zero-truncated negative binomial reaches at its mean, while the tries an uptake takes grow about as 1/K below it. A cap allows a relative rounding of 1e-12, so a fitted value a few ulps above it (uptake_calibrate() at a mean of 1000) runs. Day 99999 cannot be used in a run that reaches it because run_sim() passes every parameter explicitly, so a day set to 99999 on purpose cannot be told from the default. The exact draw keeps the count as dispersed as uptake_moments() says; an uptake reaches it with probability P(0)^10000, 37% where a positive count is 1 draw in 10,000 (LAMBDA_OOCYSTS about 1e-4) and below one in a million above a LAMBDA_OOCYSTS of about 0.003.

Alternatives considered. Clamping out-of-range values in the model: they would run as something else, unannounced. Refusing the legitimate edges too: a closed border, a null arm without subpatent infectivity and the minimum delay are real scenarios. Refusing the other spellings of a value: they mean that value, and refusing them would cost sweep cells for nothing. Capping the import rate at N_HOSTS a day: the model runs such rates, and the cap would refuse only small populations, so the rate is capped where its draw would fail, and a day likely to bring more than N_HOSTS imports warns.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-params.R (with tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R for the documented bounds) refuses each impossible value with a message that names the parameter, and stores the other spellings in SLiM’s form; tests/testthat/test-edge-values.R runs each legitimate edge to the end and checks that the run reached the state its guard handles, with the minimum delays in tests/testthat/test-treatment.R; tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R checks the exact draw’s mean and variance against uptake_moments(); tests/testthat/test-run.R runs a set at the edge of the rounding allowance on the caps.

D43 — A run started with slim -d makes the same checks and takes either spelling of a number

Decision. The model’s initialize() makes the checks of validate_params() (D42) again for a run started directly with slim -d, down to the whole numbers within ±2^53 for the counts, days and seed. Its caps allow a relative rounding of 1e-11 rather than 1e-12, because Eidos has no log1p or expm1 and so reaches the mean oocyst count by a different arithmetic route, which can differ from R’s by about 1e-12 of the cap; the wider band keeps a set R accepts from being refused there. Its messages give a float to 15 significant digits and quote a string. Not repeated: a misspelt name, which SLiM defines as a constant the model never reads; the limits on what text can carry (UTF-8, no control characters) and on numbers below 1e-300; and a SIM_DAYS outside 2 to 1e9, not finite or not a single value, which SLiM refuses itself while it reads the tick ranges, before initialize() runs (so the model’s own SIM_DAYS < 2 check is never reached), in a message that does not name SIM_DAYS. Because -d X=7 makes an Eidos integer where -d X=7.0 makes a float, and Eidos will not mix the two in rbinom(), min(), seqLen(), setSeed(), subsetting or a tick range, the model converts each parameter to the type it needs (asInteger(), asFloat()) at each such use, so either spelling gives the same run.

Why. A direct run is the one place where a typo cannot be caught in R, and each of these values would otherwise start a run that means something else, as RADCURE_MODE = 'Person' would run the per-hypnozoite mode and a probability above 1 is always true, or one that stops part-way.

Alternatives considered. Refusing one spelling, so that a float parameter must be written 7.0: a rule users would trip over. Converting each parameter once in initialize(): a constant given with -d cannot be redefined in another type.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-slim.R refuses each case in a direct run with its parameter named, and runs a five-day configuration with latency, an MDA round in the per-hypnozoite mode and a pulse of imports in both spellings, with identical events.tsv and state.tsv.

D44 — One parameter dictionary holds each parameter’s facts, and an edited set is checked when it is used

Decision. R/param-dictionary.R holds one record per parameter: its typed default, unit, meaning, single-value bounds, a joint or conditional rule in words, and its source. The defaults are taken from it; roxygen generates the Parameters section of ?vivax_params from it, and dev/update-doc-tables.R the tables of section 10 of MODEL_DESCRIPTION.md; param_info() gives it as a table, and as.data.frame() gives a parameter set’s. validate_params() is the one check (D42). A set edited with $<-, [[<- or modifyList() keeps its class and is checked in full when it is used: run_sim() and run_grid() build every set again through vivax_params(), and p <- do.call(vivax_params, p) checks one at once, as ?vivax_params says. A default taken from another parameter is set when a set is built, so editing N_FOUNDER_HOSTS leaves N_FOUNDER_LINEAGES unchanged.

Why. A parameter’s facts should be written once, where the code reads them, so that the help, the model description and the checks cannot disagree; tests hold the documented bounds to the check, the records’ types to the model’s, and the defaults to the model’s own.

Alternatives considered. A $<- method that checks each edit: every caller that adds a value to a set, run_sim() adding SEED and OUTDIR among them, and every test that builds a refused set on purpose would have to strip the class first, for a check that use already makes. Generating validate_params() from the dictionary: the joint rules are not single-value bounds, and each refusal gives its rule’s reason. Pointing section 10 at the help page: the model description is read on its own.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-param-dictionary.R: a record and one group for each parameter, the records’ types against the model’s, every documented bound against the one enforced, each refusal naming its parameter, and ?vivax_params and section 10 holding the current tables. tests/testthat/test-params.R: the defaults against the model’s defineDefault() values, each evaluated as Eidos would, and an edited set refused by run_sim().

D45 — The loaders give every run the same columns and classes, and the host rows by default

Decision. load_events() and load_state() read their file against one schema per file (R/outputs.R), the columns the model writes, in its order and classes, so every run gives the same columns in the same order and classes whatever it holds: a run with no event gives a table with no rows, a column the file lacks is added as NA of its class, a column the schema lacks follows in the file’s class, and a value that does not fit stops with the file and the column named, and its line when it is text in a column of numbers. A missing or empty file, or an argument that is not a run, is named in the error. The -1 that marks a field as not applicable is read as -1, not as NA. load_state() gives the host rows unless entity = "mosquito" or "all" asks for the mosquitoes’ or both, in the file’s order, and the columns and their classes do not depend on which rows are asked for. The same schemas, with a meaning for each column, give ?events.tsv, ?state.tsv and the tables of sections 16.1 and 16.2 of the model description.

Why. A table’s columns are part of its contract, so a reader should not have to test classes before using them; left to guess, fread() types a column by its values, and an empty file or a column holding only NA would read as logical. Most rows of state.tsv are mosquitoes, 100 of every 140 at the defaults, and a mosquito’s moi_active counts the lineages it carries, so a prevalence taken over every row mixes the two populations; the default is the rows nearly every analysis wants, and no function of the package reads the mosquito rows.

Alternatives considered. Converting the -1 sentinels to NA: analyses test != -1, and the sentinel means not applicable, not missing. Every row of state.tsv by default: it keeps the mistake easy. Separate loaders for hosts and mosquitoes: two functions for one file with one schema.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-load.R: an empty log, classes that do not depend on what a run holds, missing and extra columns, a value that does not fit, a missing or empty file, normal, extinct and never-started runs with the same columns and classes, each entity with its rows and the same classes, and the help, the loaders and the model description’s tables in agreement.

D46 — The event dictionary is the authority, and the case, episode and recurrence tables are built from it

Decision. event_types() names every event type the model writes, with its stage, whether it ends a patent episode (ends_episode) or begins one (is_onset), and a description. The package’s onset and episode-end filters are derived from those two flags, and its metrics take their cases from classify_cases(), rather than restating event names, so a new way for an episode to begin or end is picked up with no further edit. A type that cannot occur has no row: the founders are hosts and every mosquito starts uninfected, so no event seeds a mosquito. mosq_death is described as what it is, one row per genome an infected mosquito carried when it died; the deaths of uninfected mosquitoes are not logged. Built on the dictionary, classify_cases() gives one row per clone onset, founder seeding excluded, with its true origin and its episode_id, "<human_id>:<tick>", an episode being the clones that became patent in one host on one day; episodes() gives every blood-stage clone’s span from its onset to its first end, founders included; and recurrences() pairs each clone of every episode after a host’s first with each clone of the earlier episodes, or of the latest one, never with a clone of its own episode, and reads each pair’s IBD from the run’s IBD object when given it. Founder seeding is not an episode.

Why. A dictionary is read as a promise about the log, so a type that cannot occur, or a description in the wrong unit, breaks it: counted as deaths, the mosq_death rows would miss every uninfected mosquito’s death and count an infected one once per genome. The unit a recurrence study compares is the episode, and pairing row by row pairs the genotypes one bite delivered with each other. One implementation of the spans and the pairings, checked against state.tsv, spares each analysis a copy of its own, which could miss a way an episode begins or ends.

Alternatives considered. Seeding infected mosquitoes, so that a mosquito could start with a founder genotype: no analysis asks for it, and the founders are hosts by design. Logging every mosquito death: the rows of uninfected deaths would be most of a run’s log, for a number the state table already gives, since a mosquito’s age starts again at 0 when it dies. One row per episode: the genotypes of one episode differ in origin and in IBD, which a classifier needs. Founder seeding as an earlier episode: every founder host’s first acquired episode would become a recurrence, paired with an unrelated founder genome.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-load.R (the dictionary, and what mosq_death counts), tests/testthat/test-run.R (every type a run logs is in the dictionary) and tests/testthat/test-episodes.R (the fixture’s episodes, spans and pairings; with co-transmission, several clones to an episode, never paired with each other; and on a run, every clone’s span covering exactly the days it counts in moi_active); inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R checks on each configuration that every type logged is documented and every clearance matches an onset.

D47 — state.tsv counts each host’s infectious bites, which gives the EIR

Decision. Each host row of state.tsv carries infectious_bites, the bites the host received that day from a mosquito carrying a product past the EIP, whatever the bite then did (NA on mosquito rows). The model counts a bite as infectious exactly where it already draws the mosquito’s transmissible products, which come back empty exactly when no product has completed the EIP, so the count draws no random number. The count is kept on the host and reset after each day’s snapshot, since reproduction() does not run on a day with no parasite. summarise_run() reports the EIR from it as eir_per_py, infectious bites per person-year of every host over its window.

Why. The EIR is the usual measure of transmission intensity and, with prevalence, the quantity to calibrate BITING_RATE against (section 13 of the model description). Counting at the bite is exact, and per host it also gives the heterogeneity of exposure. The Ross–Macdonald formula, with the sporozoite rate read from n_transmissible, gives about 1 − 1/MOSQ_LIFESPAN of the counted EIR, about 0.9 at the default 10 days, because the snapshot is taken after the day’s mosquito deaths, and with seasonality, vector control or a boost its error can go either way (section 4.1 of the model description).

Alternatives considered. A column on the mosquito rows: the EIR is per person, and the host row is where a reader looks for exposure. A file of its own: one more output to load and document, for one number per host and day.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-model-invariants.R: where every infectious bite infects and no host is full, with case management on, each host’s infectious bites a day are its inoculations that day. tests/testthat/test-summary.R: eir_per_py is the window’s infectious bites over its person-years.

D48 — A table’s shape follows its arguments, never the run’s content

Decision. Every reader returns the same columns, in the same order and classes, with the same factor levels, on every path, whatever the run holds. force_of_infection() splits relapses into relapse (imported) and relapse (local) unless split_imported = FALSE, whether or not the run holds imports, and returns origin as a factor with all its levels; rc_by_origin() gives every origin a row; classify_travel() gives a run without imports the same columns; the IBD tables keep one column order and class whether a pair shares everything or nothing; a run with no parasite gives every reader its usual columns, with no rows where there is nothing to list, counts of 0 and NA where a quantity needs a parasite; and a table of the wrong kind is refused by name. new_infection_diversity(), which caps the genomes a window compares, draws them with its own seed, the k-th window with seed + k - 1, always under the same RNG kinds, and leaves the caller’s random stream untouched.

Why. A grid pools per-run tables, so a shape that varies with a run’s content either fails on one cell or, worse, binds by position and gives numerically plausible nonsense. An imported relapse is a distinct truth category, so relapses are split by provenance, in every run. A seeded draw lets repeat calls on one run agree, as a metric must, while the draw is unbiased in time and lineage.

Alternatives considered. Splitting relapses only in runs that hold imports: the same quantity would come back as relapse in one run and relapse (local) in another, and a pooled dcast() would put one origin in three columns without an error. Taking a window’s first genomes instead of a seeded draw: reproducible, but biased toward the window’s early genomes.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-windows.R (the same origin levels for a run with no case), tests/testthat/test-ibd.R (segment tables keep one schema), tests/testthat/test-no-parasite.R (every reader takes a run with no parasite), tests/testthat/test-inputs.R (a reader given the other kind of table says which it got) and tests/testthat/test-rng.R (a seeded draw is the same under any RNG kind, and leaves the caller’s kinds and stream alone).

D49 — Windowed series have a row for every window, divided by the days it covers, to SIM_DAYS

Decision. force_of_infection() gives one row per window of the run and per origin, with n = 0 where there is no case, and days, the days the window covers within the run: the first window holds days 1 to bin - 1, the last ends at SIM_DAYS, and rate divides by days. bin is a whole number of days, at least 1, and new_infection_diversity(bin =) gives every window of the same grid a row. Every function that summarises a window of a run takes the run’s end from SIM_DAYS, whether or not the run went extinct (D5), so the days after an extinction count as days with no parasite: prevalence and the reservoir are means over every host-day of the window, while COI and polyclonality are means over the infected host-days, NA when there are none. The per-day tables, coi_distribution() and host_state_prevalence(), report the days state.tsv holds.

Why. A window without a case is a measurement of zero, not a gap that a line or a stacked area draws straight across, and a short window divided by bin would start or end every series in a dip that is pure binning artefact; full windows are the same either way, since there days is bin. A run’s window is the period the study asks about, not the period the parasite lasted: a run that died out had no infection on its remaining days.

Alternatives considered. Dropping the partial windows: it throws away a real estimate, unbiased though noisier. Zero-filling only in the plots: every other reader of the table would meet the gaps again. Ending a run’s series at its last state row or its last case: an extinct run’s windows would be shorter, and a trailing window whose true value is zero, the most informative reading there is, would be lost. Padding state.tsv to SIM_DAYS: the file would hold rows for days the model never ran.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-windows.R: every window and origin, the days of the first and last windows, a run with no case and its plot, an extinct run’s zeros after its extinction, and the window statistics of a run that went extinct before day 200 of 400.

D50 — summarise_run() is the one summary of a run, over one window of days

Decision. summarise_run() gives one row of typed, unrounded columns named by their units (_frac, _per_py, _tick, n_), every one over the same window: days round(SIM_DAYS * burn_frac) + 1 to SIM_DAYS, the second half by default, or from and to directly. The row holds prevalence, COI and polyclonality over the window’s host-days, the reservoir, the EIR (D47), the FOI and both molFOB readings, by clone and by episode (Koepfli et al. 2013; D33), the relapse rate per person-year at risk and both relapse fractions (D28), the imported share, the counts, and the person-years and person-years at risk; the EIR, FOI and molFOB divide by the person-years of every host. It records its window, its reading (exclude_masked, which leaves the masked relapses of D26 out of every relapse column, while n_relapse_masked counts them either way) and how the run ended. A quantity with nothing to divide is NA, and a run that stopped early with no extinction or start-failure record is refused unless to is at most its last day. plot_diagnostics() takes its subtitle’s numbers and its burn-in line from the same row, and new_infection_diversity() starts on the same first day for a given burn_frac.

Why. A summary pooled over a grid must mean the same thing in every column and every cell, and the counts and denominators on the row let runs be pooled by summing them rather than by averaging rates. One definition serves the user, the dashboard and the calibration: inst/validation/calibrate_nu.R fits NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH to summarise_run()’s own columns.

Alternatives considered. Summing force_of_infection()’s rows for the FOI and molFOB: the window need not line up with its bins. A class with a print method: rbindlist() drops it. One column per masked reading: the reading is an argument, and the row records it.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-summary.R: names and classes on every kind of run; the fixture’s values over the whole run, the default window and two others; exclude_masked; extinct, never-started and unfinished runs; and on a SLiM run, every column against its definition over the window, FOI and molFOB against force_of_infection(), and the dashboard’s subtitle against the row.

D51 — host_state_prevalence() has every state on every day and counts subpatent carriers

Decision. host_state_prevalence() gives one row per day of the state table and per state, with n = 0 where no host is in it and frac its share of the day’s hosts, in five levels: uninfected, active only, active + reservoir, subpatent (a subpatent clone and no patent one, with or without hypnozoites) and reservoir only (invisible), the hosts with hypnozoites alone, whom no blood survey sees. Each row also carries the day’s mean hypnozoites per host, so the reservoir’s trajectory comes off the same table. At the default P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL = 0 no clone is subpatent, and that state is 0 throughout.

Why. A subpatent carrier is infected and can infect a mosquito, so counting it as uninfected would understate carriage exactly where treatment fails. A missing row is not a zero: without the zero rows a stacked area joins the rows on either side of an empty state and draws hosts on days that had none.

Alternatives considered. Putting subpatent carriers with hypnozoites in the reservoir-only state: they carry a blood-stage clone, which a sensitive assay would find.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-host-states.R (every state on every day, the subpatent carriers, an empty table, the reservoir on each row, the plot) and tests/testthat/test-treatment.R (on a run with recrudescence, the subpatent count is each day’s hosts with a subpatent clone and no patent one).

D52 — Transmission links follow both routes, with half weight to each parent of an outcrossed oocyst, and form the chains

Decision. transmission_links() joins each parent genome of an oocyst to each genome the oocyst’s products infected: direct, the bite’s blood stage, or liver, each relapse of the hypnozoite batch the same bite left, which carries the batch’s oocyst. Only local infections are targets: imports, founders, the relapses of an import’s batch and recrudescences can only be sources. A host’s own relapse is never linked to its earlier infection, though a mosquito that feeds on a host and later bites it makes a link like any other. Each row names both genomes and hosts, the mosquito, the oocyst, four days (the source’s onset, the feed, the bite and the target) and a weight: 1, or 1/2 for each parent of an outcrossed oocyst, so a target’s weights sum to 1. kind keeps either route, and a log cut short of the rows a link needs gives one warning. A chain is a connected component of the links taken in either direction, each source taken as the clone it came from through repeated recrudescences; each link carries its chain_id, numbered in the order of the chains’ first links, and chain_size, the chain’s genomes, founders included. A genome with no link is in no chain. The components come from a union-find with path halving.

Why. A relapse in another host is a transmission delayed by the liver, and relapses are about three in five new blood-stage clones in the model description’s representative run, so leaving liver links out would undercount onward transmission most for the infections whose batches relapse. A recrudescence is the same infection as the clone it came from (D33), so its onward transmission belongs to that clone’s chain. On the links themselves a chain can be followed and joined, and the union-find stays linear in practice where liver links make chains of thousands of genomes.

Alternatives considered. One row per target: it loses the second parent of an outcrossed oocyst. Carrying a target’s detected or into_patent_lineage on its link: classify_cases() holds a case’s attributes, and the help gives the join. Label propagation with pointer jumping for the chains: it hooks nodes, not roots, so it needs about as many passes as a chain is long. A chain of its own for each unlinked genome: an edge table cannot hold it, and classify_chain() labels every case with its introduction (D41).

How to check. tests/testthat/test-transmission.R: the fixture’s links, targets and weights, a self link, kind, empty and cut logs, the chains of each kind with a recrudescence kept with its clone, the components against a reference union-find on long, disjoint, star and random graphs, and on a run, every local case the target of one transmission and the chains partitioning the linked genomes. inst/validation/audit_events_and_ibd.R: its transmission-link checks on each configuration.

D53 — Rc is the case reproduction number by true origin, each secondary case counted once

Decision. rc_by_origin() gives the mean number of secondary cases each case caused (Fraser 2007), by the case’s true origin. A case is a clone onset, a row of classify_cases(); its secondary cases are the targets of its links through both routes (D52), each counted once, so one from an outcrossed oocyst credits 1/2 to each parent. kind chooses the routes, and direct and liver add up to all. The function takes the run: from and followup choose the onsets counted, from day from to SIM_DAYS - followup, both 0 by default. With unit = "acquisition" a recrudescence is not a case, and its onward transmission is credited to the clone it re-expanded from, through repeated recrudescences. Every origin keeps a row, with n_cases, n_secondary, Rc and onward_frac unrounded, and Rc and onward_frac NA where there is no case.

Why. A case reproduction number counts what each case actually caused, which the links record exactly. Half credit counts each secondary case once, so that Rc sits near 1 at a self-sustaining steady state, above 1 while an epidemic grows from its founders, and lower where imports sustain transmission. A case near the end of a run has had less time to transmit, above all through relapses: a hypnozoite stays dormant 1/(ALPHA_ACTIVATE + MU_HYPNOZOITE) days on average, about four months at the defaults, and more than a year for 1 in 20.

Alternatives considered. Full credit to both parents of an outcrossed oocyst: it counts such a secondary case twice. A default follow-up: the right one depends on the run’s phase, which the help explains. An events table and a separate run length as arguments: the run gives both.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-transmission.R: the fixture’s values for both units, half credit and the recrudescence walked back; the routes adding up; a run with no case; from and followup and their refusals; and on a run, the counts as the weights of the links from cases.

D54 — One function per question, every reader takes a run, and no plumbing is exported

Decision. Each export answers one question, and a function whose own help would tell the user not to use it is not exported. Plumbing is internal: SLiM’s path and installed version, which check_setup() shows; the builder of SLiM’s arguments, which run_sim() uses; and the plot theme, which every plot applies. Every reader takes a run, a vivax_run or its directory, and a plot takes a run or, where it draws one function’s table, that table; a table of the other kind is refused by name. One naming rule holds throughout: from and to for a window, n for a count, _frac for a share from 0 to 1, and every table a reader returns a data.table. example_run() returns a small run that ships with the package, 60 hosts for 400 days with imports, treatment, recrudescence and co-transmission, so that every kind of case, recurrence and link occurs in it; data-raw/example_run.R makes it from the settings in R/example.R.

Why. A user looking for how to answer a question should find one function, and plumbing is only more to learn: a methods section needs the SLiM version a run ran on, which every run records (load_run()$slim_version), and a user restyles a plot with ggplot2’s own themes. One convention lets any reader be pointed at a run. The bundled run lets the examples, the vignettes and a first look run without SLiM, and the tests that compare it with its settings and with the model fail when a default or the model changes, until it is made again.

How to check. tests/testthat/test-exports.R lists the exports exactly; tests/testthat/test-inputs.R gives every reader a run and every plot a run or its table, and each the wrong kind of table; tests/testthat/test-example-run.R checks that the shipped run is this model’s run of its settings and holds every kind of case, recurrence and link.
